dimension: Visual design direction: editorial, custom look for a premium but approachable salon and day spa (typography, layout, color depth within a fixed palette, motion, photography, iconography, avoiding a template look, reference sites, mockup critique)

recommendations.title: Fix the palette's contrast failures before any styling: gold is not a text color on cream, and white on gold fails
recommendations.detail: I measured the current palette against WCAG. Gold #b8985f on cream #faf8f5 is 2.57:1, which fails. White on a gold button is 2.73:1, which also fails, and the mockup's buttons all use it. Gold-dk #9c7f4c on cream is 3.57:1, so it only passes for large text. Ink #1c1c1c on gold is 6.24:1, and gold on ink is 6.24:1, both passing. Rules: (1) Primary button: gold background with ink text (6.24:1), hover to ink background with gold text. Or use gold-dk as the background with white text only at 18px+/bold, since 3.78:1 is borderline. (2) Eyebrows, links and small gold labels on light grounds use a deeper shade of the same gold. #846a3a is 4.83:1 and #7a6232 is 5.47:1 on cream, so it is the same hue with no new color. Keep #b8985f for rules, large display numerals, icons and anything placed on ink. (3) Body text #6b6b6b is 5.03:1 on cream but only 4.53:1 on a darker sand tint. Darken body copy to about #555 (7.0:1) for phone readability and use it at weight 400, not 300. Open Sans 300 at 16px, the current setting, is too thin on phones.
recommendations.evidence: Contrast ratios computed from the hex values (WCAG 2.x relative luminance): b8985f/faf8f5 = 2.57; fff/b8985f = 2.73; 1c1c1c/b8985f = 6.24; 846a3a/faf8f5 = 4.83; 7a6232/faf8f5 = 5.47; 555/faf8f5 = 7.03. The mockup's gold eyebrow labels and white-on-gold buttons both fall under the 4.5:1 AA threshold for text.

recommendations.title: Build depth from tints, shades and a dark 'ink' mode, with no new hues
recommendations.detail: Derive a tonal ramp from the fixed palette and use it for section rhythm. Suggested tokens: --paper #faf8f5 (base), --sand #f1ece3 (alternate band, a cream tinted toward line), --line #e7e2d9 (hairlines, 1px rules), --gold-ink #846a3a (text-safe gold), --gold #b8985f (ornament and on-dark), --gold-dk #9c7f4c (hover), --ink #1c1c1c (dark sections), --ink-2 #262420 (a card on ink, ink warmed with a touch of gold), --on-ink #e7e2d9 (body on ink, 13.2:1). Section rhythm down the homepage: paper, sand, INK (team), paper, INK (final booking band) and footer. The dark sections give weight and luxury without a new color. Add texture instead of hue: a pre-rendered 128px tiled PNG noise at 4 to 6% opacity with mix-blend-mode:multiply on paper/sand, and soft-light on ink. Use PNG rather than a live feTurbulence filter, because SVG filters are GPU-heavy on phones. Use gold only as a 'thread': 1px rules, numerals, the Book button and underline hovers. Keep it to about 5% of pixels so it stays precious.
recommendations.evidence: CSS-Tricks and freeCodeCamp document the feTurbulence grain technique. Ultimate Design Tools: 'Subtle noise (5-15% opacity) adds organic texture'. It also warns that SVG filters 'can be GPU-intensive, especially on mobile' and recommends a pre-rendered tiled PNG. Aesop's site (Work & Co / siteinspire) gets its whole luxury feel from a neutral charcoal plus warm beige system with no accent explosion.

recommendations.title: Typography: keep Prata as the brand voice, but give it an italic partner and a better body face
recommendations.detail: Prata has no italic, so the mockup's 'tailored to you.' cannot be made with Prata. Options, all on Google Fonts, which the site already loads: (A, lowest risk) keep Prata for H1/H2 and add Instrument Serif Italic or Cormorant Garamond Italic 500 only for the 1 to 3 italic accent words per headline. (B, most distinctive) replace Prata with Fraunces variable (opsz, wght, SOFT axes; opsz 144, SOFT 50, wght 300 to 400 for display) plus its true italic. One file covers display and accent, and the SOFT axis gives warmth that reads 'approachable', not 'cold couture'. Body: swap Open Sans for a warmer, more current sans such as Manrope, Hanken Grotesk or DM Sans at weight 400, 17 to 18px, line-height 1.6, measure 60 to 68ch. Scale: fluid with clamp() (Utopia method), from ratio 1.2 at 360px to 1.333 at 1440px. H1 about clamp(2.6rem, 1.6rem + 4.2vw, 5.4rem), line-height 1.02 to 1.08, letter-spacing -0.01 to -0.02em, which tightens the display type. Use text-wrap: balance on headings and text-wrap: pretty on paragraphs. Small caps eyebrows at 0.72 to 0.78rem, tracking 0.18 to 0.22em, in the sans (not Prata), color --gold-ink. Numerals: use the display serif large for '2009', '28' and '#1' as typographic objects instead of icons. Load at most 2 families and 4 files, with font-display: swap and preload the H1 face.
recommendations.evidence: MadeGood 2026 font trends: 'Expressive Variable Serifs' (Fraunces named) and Anti-Geometric Editorial Serifs lead. It also notes aggressive serif italics 'peaked in 2024' and are 'now reading as predictable', which argues for fewer, more deliberate italics. Heather Jones pairs Prata with Work Sans for 'oversized photography, neutral colors, and lots of white space' and Fraunces with Manrope. Search summaries describe Instrument Serif as 'Cormorant elegance but more contemporary'. Utopia: 'define a type scale for a small screen, define a type scale for a large screen, tell the browser to interpolate.'

recommendations.title: Italic accent system: one italic phrase per section, never decorative script over photos
recommendations.detail: Use a consistent rule: each H1/H2 may italicize one short phrase that carries the emotional turn. Examples: 'Beauty & relaxation, *tailored to you.*', 'Two sisters. *One chair a week, still.*', 'Voted Licking County's *No. 1 spa* since 2016.' Italic in the same gold-ink or in ink. Drop the handwritten script fonts ('Good Hair Brighter Days', 'Beauty Looks Good On You', 'Right here in Newark'). They are the most 'Canva template' signal in the mockup and fail legibility over photos. If a human mark is wanted, use one real element: scan Lisa and Ashley's actual signatures as SVG under Our Story. That is authentic, not a font.
recommendations.evidence: MadeGood lists 'Anti-AI Handwriting' as authentic human marks, which only work when they are real. Its note that stock serif italics are becoming predictable argues for scarcity. The prior assistant review already flagged script overlays as hard to read over busy photos.

recommendations.title: Layout: a 12-column editorial grid with deliberate asymmetry, left-aligned text and one 'break' per section
recommendations.detail: Use CSS grid with 12 columns and max content 1320px, but let images bleed to the viewport edge on one side (grid-column: full-start / col-7). Patterns to use: (1) Hero as a 5/7 split, with text left-aligned on paper and the image bleeding off the right edge in a tall portrait crop (4:5), not a full-bleed background with text laid over it. (2) Headings left-aligned and offset: an H2 spanning cols 1 to 7, with the intro paragraph dropped to cols 8 to 12 and baseline-aligned to the H2's last line (the mockup does this once; make it the system). (3) One overlap per section at most: a caption card or numeral overlapping an image edge by 48 to 80px, or a portrait nudged down 10% to break the row. (4) Vertical rhythm: section padding clamp(72px, 10vw, 160px), and use whitespace instead of boxes. No card borders or shadows; separate items with 1px --line hairlines. (5) Number the sections quietly ('01 Services', '02 Team') in the eyebrow. That is an editorial and magazine cue. (6) Centered text only in the final booking band. Everywhere else, left-aligned.
recommendations.evidence: Aesop (Awwwards and siteinspire analysis): 'a mix of vertical and horizontal framing, mimicking the feel of a high-end print editorial or gallery catalog.' siteinspire tags its best cosmetics sites 'Typographic', 'Grid Layout', 'Unusual Layout'. Odyssée Clinic (siteinspire) uses numbered pillars and generous whitespace. This Is Also: 'layer authored choices on top of proven structures.'

recommendations.title: Replace the '6 photo tiles' services mosaic with a typographic service index
recommendations.detail: There are no good in-service photos yet, and the mockup's 6-tile mosaic depends on them. It is also the most template-like section. Build instead a large typographic list, like a menu or table of contents: each row is a full-width link with a big serif service name (Hair, Nails, Skin & Facials, Massage, Brides, Makeup & Brows, Waxing, Spray Tans, Men's, Slay Aesthetics). Beside it, in the sans, sit a one-line descriptor and a real 'from $' price pulled from the service pages (e.g. 'Women's cut from $37', 'Gel manicure from $44', 'Relaxation massage from $42', 'Signature facial from $90', 'Spray tan $35'), then an arrow. Separate rows with 1px line rules. On hover (desktop), a single image follows or crossfades in a fixed slot at the right. On mobile, show a small 56px thumbnail. Showing prices up front differentiates the site and helps clicks, because most salon sites hide them. When real photos arrive, they drop into the hover slot without any layout change.
recommendations.evidence: This Is Also recommends 'cursor awareness' and micro-interactions that respond to behavior as the differentiator on top of proven structures. Sticklight and The Nerd Stack both argue that original, real imagery converts and stock imagery 'kills credibility', which argues against filling a mosaic with stock.

recommendations.title: Put the team on an ink section so the black-background headshots bleed seamlessly
recommendations.detail: All 28 headshots are shot on a near-black backdrop with staff in black. On a cream page they read as 28 dark boxes. On an --ink #1c1c1c section they dissolve into the ground and look like a commissioned editorial portrait series. Do this: a full-width ink section with an H2 in cream/gold ('28 specialists. *One* standard.'). Then show a horizontal, scroll-snapping row or an asymmetric grid of 5 to 8 portraits at 3:4 with a slight bottom gradient to ink. Below each: name in serif, then level and specialty in small caps (e.g. 'Devon, Salon Manager and Director of Education: hand-sewn extensions, blonding'). Each links to the existing dialog.bio. Hover effect: a 1.03 scale on the image and a gold underline drawing across the name. Grade all portraits identically (slight warm tone, same black point) so the set reads as one series.
recommendations.evidence: Observed in the project assets: team/*.jpg are 720x960 studio headshots on black, and join-1.jpg shows the whole staff dressed in black. Salon guides: 'clients often book a person, not just a business', and 'A grid of consistently lit, consistently cropped... reads as professional.'

recommendations.title: Replace the icon trust row with typographic proof
recommendations.detail: The mockup's 4-icon trust bar (calendar, people, heart, leaf icons) is a textbook template pattern. Replace it with a quiet horizontal band of 3 or 4 large serif numerals with small-caps captions, all verifiable: '2009 Founded by sisters Lisa and Ashley', '#1 Spa in Licking County, voted every year since 2016', '28 Stylists, nail artists, therapists and a CNP', '5,500 sq ft Grew from an 1,800 sq ft house'. Separate them with vertical 1px gold rules. This doubles as E-E-A-T proof (experience, and years of local recognition). Drop the generic 'a more beautiful you, always'.
recommendations.evidence: This Is Also and Ruthless Reviews identify 'rounded-square icons' and 'three-card grid' as core template signifiers. Big numerals as typographic objects are a 2026 editorial device (MadeGood: display serifs dominate hero headlines).

recommendations.title: Restrained motion: three motion ideas, used consistently, all disabled under reduced-motion
recommendations.detail: Pick three motion ideas and apply them everywhere. (1) Reveal: section content fades up 16px over 600ms with cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), staggered 60ms, triggered once via IntersectionObserver (or CSS animation-timeline: view() as progressive enhancement). (2) Image unmask: key editorial images reveal with clip-path inset(8% 0 0 0) to inset(0) plus a 1.06 to 1 scale over 900ms. (3) Links and buttons: a gold underline that draws left to right (background-size 0 to 100% over 250ms), the button arrow nudging 4px, and a hover color swap from gold to ink. Micro-feedback stays under 300ms. No parallax on text, no auto-playing carousels, no scroll-jacking, no cursor followers. Wrap all of it in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), so the default is static. Animate only transform and opacity. A sticky header shrinks from 88 to 64px on scroll, with a hairline appearing.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g: 'Motion is most often appropriate as a form of subtle feedback for microinteractions, rather than to induce delight or entertain users', and it warns against multiple simultaneous animations. Work & Co on Aesop: 'Elegant motion design creates calm transitions that mirror a relaxing in-store experience.' 2025 and 2026 motion guides: 'Keep delightful touches fast (<300ms)... respect reduced motion', 'Prefer transforms and opacity.'

recommendations.title: Photography art direction: a written brief so new photos match
recommendations.detail: Write a one-page shot brief. Light: soft window light or a large softbox from one side, warm white balance (about 4500 to 5000K), no ring-light glare on faces. Palette in frame: cream, black and brushed brass, which echo the web palette (the team already wears black). Subjects: hands and tools mid-service (foils, a brush on a nail, a gua sha on skin), 3/4 over-the-shoulder shots of a stylist and client, and a 'reveal' at the mirror. Crops: tall 4:5 and 3:4 portraits for the hero and editorial, 1:1 for detail. Leave negative space on one side for type. Grading: one Lightroom preset (lifted blacks to about 8%, muted saturation -10, warm midtones) applied to everything, including the existing headshots and room photos, so old and new cohere. Before and afters: same angle, same light, same background and same crop, side by side as a pair, never a slider. Also shoot the exterior at golden hour, Lisa and Ashley together, and details (product shelf with the real brands, the front desk, the boutique). Ask each stylist before using their Instagram photos, and get client consent for any face.
recommendations.evidence: Phorest shot list: team, location, 'action shots (shampooing, treatments, reveals)', detail shots; 'establish brand adjectives... build a mood board'; 'Keep adjustments minimal.' Salon photo guides: 'A grid of consistently lit, consistently cropped before-and-after shots reads as professional'; a real client photo beat the best stock image in a Marketing Experiments A/B test. Mangomint, on GBY Beauty: 'up-close imagery shows off exactly how good they are.'

recommendations.title: Make the existing weak photos usable through treatment, not by hiding them
recommendations.detail: Until the new shoot: (a) Crop the empty-room photos (mani room, facial room, massage room) tightly to details, such as a towel stack, a lamp or a chair edge. Apply the shared grade and show them small (in the service-index hover slot) rather than as big tiles. (b) Use join-1.jpg, the full team in black, as a wide 'About' image with a caption such as 'The Bellezza & Co. team, Newark'. Its vignette filter should be neutralized. (c) Duotone-ish treatment: a CSS filter such as sepia(.15) saturate(.85) contrast(1.02) plus a thin gold-tinted overlay (gold at 8%, multiply) gives old photos a common look. (d) Retire hero-1/hero-2 cotton flat-lays and the candle and lily tiles completely; they are the clearest stock signal.
recommendations.evidence: DesignRush: 'Good creative direction isn't about where an image came from, it's about what you do with it.' The Nerd Stack: visitors 'can usually tell when a photo is stock.'

recommendations.title: Iconography: almost none; use a single thin-line set only for utility
recommendations.detail: Use icons only where they speed recognition: phone, map pin, clock, calendar, Instagram, Facebook, arrow and close. Use one set (e.g. Phosphor Light or Lucide at 1.25px stroke) inlined as SVG with currentColor, sized to the text cap-height. Remove all decorative icons from content sections (no heart, leaf or scissors icons in service lists or trust rows). The B&Co monogram from the logo can serve as the single brand ornament: a small gold mark at section starts or as a favicon and loader, used sparingly.
recommendations.evidence: 'Rounded-square icons' and icon rows are listed among the core template signifiers (Ruthless Reviews and This Is Also). Gielly Green, an Awwwards E-commerce Honoree in Jan 2026, uses a minimal SVG icon set plus its monogram as the main brand device.

recommendations.title: Booking stays visible without cluttering: a sticky header CTA and a mobile bottom bar
recommendations.detail: Desktop: the sticky header keeps the 'Book' button (gold background, ink text) at the right, with a secondary text link, 'Gift cards', beside it. Mobile: a fixed bottom bar with 2 actions, 'Book online' (primary, links to Meevo) and 'Call' (tel:740-366-1604), with padding-bottom env(safe-area-inset-bottom). It appears after the hero scrolls out and hides while the footer is visible. Put 'New here? Take the 60-second match quiz' (Mya) as a secondary path in the hero and in the service index. The quiz is a real differentiator; Gielly Green uses a similar 'Tailor Your Ritual' quiz.
recommendations.evidence: Mangomint's spa roundup repeatedly credits an 'easy-to-spot Book Now' button, and Cheeks + Co gives Book Now 'top billing as the first menu item'. Glasskin repeats BOOK NOW in the nav, sticky header and section heads. Gielly Green places a quiz CTA ('Tailor Your Ritual') alongside booking.

recommendations.title: No carousels: before and afters, and later reviews, as static editorial layouts
recommendations.detail: The mockup has two carousels (before and afters, testimonials). Replace them with static layouts. Transformations: an asymmetric grid of 3 to 4 pairs. One is large (the brow lamination graphic works now), with 2 or 3 smaller pairs added as real photos arrive, each captioned with the service and the stylist's name (linking to their bio), which ties the work to named experts. Reviews: until real reviews exist, show none. Later, feature one large pull-quote in serif italic with the reviewer's first name and last initial, the service and the stylist, plus a link to the Meevo Five Star ratings page and the Google reviews count. A single well-set quote reads as editorial; three in a row reads as template.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g: 'People often immediately scroll past these large images', and most users see only the first frame. It recommends static alternatives and 'never rely solely on carousels for important content.'

recommendations.title: Reference sites to study, and what to take from each
recommendations.detail: Aesop (aesop.com; Work & Co; Awwwards and siteinspire): a neutral charcoal and beige system, packaging-derived type, calm transitions. Take the tonal restraint and gallery-catalog framing. Gielly Green (giellygreen.co.uk; Awwwards E-commerce Honors, Jan 2026): monogram-led nav with Book now always present, a quiz ('Tailor Your Ritual') and punchy fragment headlines. Take persistent booking and a quiz as a first-class path. Odyssée Clinic (odysseeclinic.com.au; Nightjar; siteinspire): numbered philosophy pillars, one strong face-led hero, heavy whitespace, 'Book Consultation' fixed in the nav. Take numbered editorial sections. Salon Heleen Hülsmann (Twntytwo; Awwwards HM, Jul 2025): a two-color taupe and off-white system proves a tiny palette can feel luxe; take the two-tone discipline. Susanne Kaufmann, Remedy and Hyeja (siteinspire cosmetics category, tagged Typographic, Minimal and Grid Layout): large type, product-as-object crops. GBY Beauty and Glasskin (Mangomint roundup): close-up, real-work imagery, and booking repeated at section heads. Treat Awwwards 'salon' winners from 2011 to 2020 (Westend, Rela, Salon Sona, Base Coat) as dated; Sona's WebGL and vertical menu is the kind of spectacle to avoid for a local salon.
recommendations.evidence: Fetched the Awwwards salon nominees list (Heleen Hülsmann HM Jul 17 2025; Gielly Green E-commerce Honors Jan 2026; The Proof HM Aug 2024; Qiqi SOTD Aug 2023; Base Coat HM 2020; Rela HM 2019), the siteinspire cosmetics category, the Work & Co Aesop case study, the Odyssée homepage and Mangomint's roundup. Lapa Ninja's beauty category (137 examples) returned 403 to the fetcher, so it is referenced but not analysed.

recommendations.title: Pick one signature move competitors would never make
recommendations.detail: Candidate: 'The Menu' concept. The whole site is typeset like a printed salon menu or editorial price list, with hairline rules, dotted leaders between service and price, and small-caps level labels (Associate / Senior / Expert / Master) as a consistent visual legend. It fits the existing .price-item markup and the build-schema.py contract, so it is cheap to execute. Then the homepage service index, the service pages and even the team levels share one distinctive typographic system. Secondary candidate: the ink team wall. Commit to one as the brand's signature and repeat it.
recommendations.evidence: This Is Also: 'Pick the one decision your competitors would never make and commit to it.' Aesop's system derives from its packaging; the salon's own 'packaging' is its menu.

recommendations.title: Critique of the mockup as a starting point: keep the bones, change the details
recommendations.detail: KEEP: the cream and ink warmth; the utility top bar; logo left with 5-item nav and a persistent Book button; the split hero with a serif headline and italic turn; left-aligned H2s with an offset intro paragraph; the quiz band as a real path; the Our Story section with the sisters; the visit block with hours and a map; the dark final booking band. CHANGE: (1) White-on-gold buttons fail contrast (2.73:1); use ink on gold. (2) Gold eyebrows fail on cream (2.57:1); use #846a3a. (3) The hero depends on a photo you do not have. Launch with a typographic hero: a large H1 across 7 columns and, at right, the full-team photo cropped, or an owner portrait pair from the two headshots set side by side on ink. (4) The trust bar uses icons plus a filler slogan; swap in typographic numerals with verified facts (2009, #1 Licking County since 2016, 28 team, 5,500 sq ft). (5) The six-tile services mosaic needs six photos you don't have and reads as template; use the typographic service index with from-prices. (6) Both carousels (transformations, testimonials) go static, and testimonials are omitted until real ones exist. (7) Four script overlays go; replace with the real signatures of Lisa and Ashley only. (8) Team portraits on cream look boxed; move the team to an ink section. (9) '20+ beauty professionals' should say 28, which is true and more specific. (10) All fabricated data (phone 522-4173, 200 Deo Drive, the hours, Kelsey, Morgan, Abby and Tori, the Emily R., Jessica M. and Caitlin B. quotes, the AI storefront and before-and-after images, (c) 2024) is replaced with verified facts. (11) The service list omits Brides-as-its-own-path emphasis (bridal coordinator, travel team) and Men's care; add them. (12) The footer is thin; add hours, address, phone, gift cards, careers, policies, app badges and the brands carried.
recommendations.evidence: Direct inspection of 1.png against the business facts and the contrast calculations above. NN/g on carousels; template-signifier sources.

pitfalls: The 'stock hero, 3 icon cards, testimonial carousel, CTA band' sequence. Any section that could be moved to a dentist's site unchanged is template. Every section must contain a Bellezza-specific fact, name, number or photo.
Everything centered. Center only the final booking band; left-align all body and headings.
Decorative icon rows (heart, leaf, scissors, calendar), rounded-square icon badges and generic 'quality / care / relax' triplets.
Script and handwriting fonts laid over photos (legibility, and a Canva-template signal). Use real signatures or nothing.
White text on #b8985f (2.73:1) and gold text on cream (2.57:1). Both fail WCAG AA; the mockup does both.
Open Sans at weight 300 and grey #6b6b6b body on sand: too faint on phones. Use weight 400 and a darker grey.
Auto-rotating carousels, before/after drag sliders, parallax text, scroll-jacking, cursor followers, WebGL gimmicks, and animating on every element.
Mixing old stock (cotton flat-lays, candles, lilies) with real team photos. One stock image undermines the credibility of all the real ones.
Mismatched photo grading. Real photos from 5 sources must share one preset, or the page looks assembled from parts.
Fabricated or AI-generated reviews, before and afters, storefronts or staff. Trust is destroyed instantly if a local client notices, and fake reviews can break FTC rules.
Card containers with drop shadows and rounded 16px corners everywhere (the Tailwind/SaaS look). Use hairlines and whitespace instead.
Too many italics. The 2024 'serif italic everywhere' look now reads predictable; limit to one phrase per heading.
Loading 3+ font families or many weights. Keep to 2 families, preload the H1 face, and use font-display: swap for LCP.
Hiding prices. For a local salon, 'from $' prices on the homepage build trust and qualify clicks.
A hamburger-only nav on desktop. Keep 5 visible items plus Book.
bellezza_specific: Tokens to add in :root without new hues: --paper #faf8f5, --sand #f1ece3, --line #e7e2d9, --gold #b8985f (ornament and on-ink), --gold-ink #846a3a (text-safe gold on light, 4.83:1), --gold-dk #9c7f4c (hover), --ink #1c1c1c, --ink-2 #262420, --on-ink #e7e2d9, --text #555 (7.0:1 on paper). Buttons: gold background with ink text, hover to ink background with gold text.

Homepage order proposal: utility bar, then header (logo, Services / Meet the Team / New Guests / Brides / About, plus Book). Hero: a typographic H1 'Beauty & relaxation, *tailored to you.*' with Book online, Take the match quiz, and 'or call 740-366-1604'; image at right, with the team photo or owner pair as a placeholder until the shoot. Then: numerals band (2009 / #1 since 2016 / 28 / 5,500 sq ft). '01 Services' as a typographic index with from-prices. '02 The team' on INK with the black-background headshots. '03 Our story' with Lisa and Ashley's headshots side by side, the 1,800 to 5,500 sq ft story, 'still behind the chair one day a week', and real signatures. '04 Brides' band (coordinator, travel team). Brands-we-carry strip (Dermalogica, Olaplex and the rest) in greyscale logos at 40% opacity. Visit block (206 Deo Drive, real hours, map, holiday closures link). INK final Book band. Rich footer.

The team headshots are on black, and join-1 shows everyone in black. That makes an ink team section the single highest-impact, zero-cost design move; it turns existing assets into an editorial portrait series.

Launch hero without a new photo: set a large Prata or Fraunces H1 over 7 columns. At right, place ashley-basham.jpg and lisa-jeffries.jpg as a slightly offset pair on an ink panel, captioned 'Lisa & Ashley, founders, since 2009'. Swap in a real stylist-with-client shot when available.

The typographic service index with from-prices ('Women's cut from $37', 'Gel manicure from $44', 'Relaxation massage from $42', 'Signature facial from $90', 'Brazilian wax from $75', 'Spray tan $35') replaces the photo mosaic and uses real data already on the service pages.

'Menu' signature style for service pages: .menu-group > h3 as a serif section head with a gold hairline, .price-item rows with dotted leaders between span.name and span.price, and level labels (Associate / Senior / Expert / Master) in small caps with a legend at the top. This is compatible with tools/build-schema.py.
Stylist levels could become a visual legend: 5 small gold ticks for Jr Associate to Master shown on team cards and price tables. This explains pricing and signals expertise (E-E-A-T) in one device.
Retire hero-1.jpg, hero-2.jpg and the tile candle and lily images entirely. Show the empty-room photos only as small, graded, tightly cropped details.

Brow lamination before/after graphic: re-crop to a matched pair on sand with a caption naming the service. It becomes the first 'Transformations' item; add stylist Instagram work (with permission) as a static grid, not a carousel.
Mobile: fixed bottom bar with 'Book online' (Meevo link) and 'Call' (tel:7403661604), shown after the hero and hidden near the footer. Respect env(safe-area-inset-bottom).

Fonts: either keep Prata and add Instrument Serif Italic (or Cormorant Garamond Italic) for accent phrases, or move to Fraunces variable (with italic), with Manrope or Hanken Grotesk 400 replacing Open Sans 300. Keep to 2 families via the existing Google Fonts @import, converted to a preconnect plus link in the head for speed.
Motion budget: fade-up reveal, image clip-path unmask and gold underline hover only, all inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and implemented in site.js with a single IntersectionObserver.

dimension: Conversion and booking UX for salon, spa and beauty websites (2024-2026): CTA placement and copy, the handoff to Meevo, service menu presentation, first-time client paths, gift cards, social proof, tap-to-call, open-now hours, forms

recommendations.title: One primary action everywhere: 'Book an appointment', linked straight to Meevo
recommendations.detail: Every Book CTA (header, hero, service-page menus, team bios, final dark band, mobile bar) should link directly to https://login.meevo.com/bellezza/ob?locationId=103245. Right now the nav's 'Book Online' goes to book-online.html first, which adds a step. Keep book-online.html as a helper page ('How online booking works', the app badges, the policies summary, the phone number), but do not route buttons through it. Use one visual style for the primary button throughout. Use ink text #1c1c1c on gold #b8985f (6.24:1 contrast). White text on gold is only 2.73:1, which fails WCAG AA. Keep secondary actions (Explore services, Call, Gift cards) as outline or text buttons so gold always means 'book'. Put the CTA URLs in the single config object in site.js (it already holds booking, tel and giftcards) so every page shares them.
recommendations.evidence: Booking tools cite roughly 7% more abandonment for each extra step or required field (ReWork / Zenoti booking-flow guidance). Zenoti's Nov 2025 survey of 1,000+ US salon-goers found 71% had decided against booking because it was hard to reach someone or book online, and 75% say easier booking makes them more likely to stay loyal. The median salon takes 26% of bookings online vs 61% for top performers (Zenoti 2026 Benchmark). White on #b8985f measures 2.73:1 and #1c1c1c on #b8985f measures 6.24:1 (computed with the WCAG formula).

recommendations.title: Mobile sticky bottom action bar: Book + Call
recommendations.detail: Below about 768px, fix a bar to the bottom of the screen with two thumb-reachable targets: 'Book an appointment' (gold, about 65% of the width) and 'Call' (outline, tel:+17403661604, phone icon plus the word 'Call'). Make it at least 56px tall plus padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Give it an opaque background (#fff or #000 with a hairline #e7e2d9 top border) and add matching body padding-bottom so it never hides the footer. Hide it while the dark 'Book your appointment' band or the footer is in view (IntersectionObserver) so two book buttons don't stack. Do not animate it in and out on every scroll. On desktop, rely on a compact sticky header with the gold Book button instead. The bar goes on every page, including the service menus, because that is where visitors decide.
recommendations.evidence: Hoober's field study of 1,300+ phone users found 49% hold the phone one-handed and use their thumb, which makes the bottom of the screen the easiest area to reach. Secondary summaries of Baymard research report 5-12% mobile conversion lifts from sticky purchase bars. We could not fetch Baymard's original, so treat that figure as directional. Google/Ipsos found 70% of mobile searchers have used click-to-call, and 47% are more likely to try another brand when they can't call directly. Mobile abandonment runs 85.65% vs 73.76% on desktop (cross-industry figure cited by Zoca).

recommendations.title: Compact, opaque sticky header; the utility bar scrolls away
recommendations.detail: Let the black top utility bar (address, phone, gift cards, socials) scroll off the screen. Keep only the main header sticky: logo, five nav items, and the gold Book button, about 64-72px tall on desktop and 56-60px on mobile. Give it a solid cream or white background with a bottom border. No transparent or blurred header over photos. On mobile, either keep the header always visible (a hamburger plus a small Book button) or have it hide on scroll-down and reappear on scroll-up with a 300-400ms slide, not both. Make sure anchor targets have a scroll-margin-top equal to the header height so jump links don't land under the header.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g's sticky-header guidelines say to keep it small, give it an opaque background that contrasts with the content, use minimal or no animation, and use a 300-400ms slide-in for partially persistent headers. They also note sticky headers can take up 30%+ of the viewport on zoomed mobile screens.

recommendations.title: Hero: a clear booking decision in the first screen
recommendations.detail: The hero should hold the headline, a 1-2 sentence value line with specifics ('Hair, nails, skin and massage from a 28-person team in Newark since 2009'), a primary 'Book an appointment' button and a secondary 'Explore services' link. Directly under the buttons, add one line of proof: 'Voted #1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016', plus 'Open today until 8pm' pulled from the live hours logic. Use a still image, not an auto-rotating slider. On mobile, show the headline and both CTAs before the image, or overlay only if contrast is 4.5:1 or better. Don't set headline copy in the script font.
recommendations.evidence: In NN/g's 2018 eyetracking study (120 users, 130k fixations), 57% of viewing time was above the fold and 74% within the first two screens. NN/g also found auto-forwarding carousels hurt task success: users missed offers even when the target was the first slide, and on mobile the slide changes after users have already scrolled past.

recommendations.title: CTA copy: specific verbs; keep the booking button label the same everywhere
recommendations.detail: Use 'Book an appointment' (hero, bottom band) and 'Book now' (header or mobile bar only, where space is tight). Use contextual labels on menus: 'Book a massage', 'Book a facial', 'Book nails'. Use 'Call 740-366-1604' rather than a bare icon. For the quiz, use 'Find my stylist' or 'Take the 60-second match quiz' (check how long the Mya quiz actually takes before naming a duration). For gift cards, use 'Buy an eGift card' or 'Send a gift card'. Avoid vague labels ('Learn more', 'Click here', 'Submit'). Add a small reassurance line under the main CTA: 'Book online 24/7 or call us. Changes need 24 hours' notice.'
recommendations.evidence: Aagaard's ContentVerve/Unbounce test found first-person copy ('my') beat 'your' by 90% in click-through. Replications range from 30% to 90%, and one payment-page test went the other way (-25%). So write specific first-person copy for low-commitment actions (quizzes) and test it, and use plain action verbs for booking. NN/g's link-writing guideline is that links should be descriptive and start with the keyword.

recommendations.title: Smooth the handoff to Meevo
recommendations.detail: (1) Tell people what's next: in the booking microcopy, say 'You'll choose your service, provider and time on our secure booking page (Meevo). First visit? You'll create a quick account.' (2) Open Meevo in the same tab. NN/g advises against new tabs, especially on mobile. If you use a new tab anyway, mark it visibly and add rel=noopener. (3) Add UTM tags to every booking link (for example ?locationId=103245&utm_source=website&utm_medium=cta&utm_content=hero|header|mobilebar|salon-menu) so you can see which placement drives bookings. Meevo already appends utm_* for its Google Book Now integration, but test once that extra parameters don't break the booking page. (4) Turn on Meevo's 'Google Book Online' button in MeevoXchange > Integrations so people can book from the Google Business Profile. The business name and address must match exactly. (5) Link the iOS/Android app badges near booking for returning clients. (6) Ask about Meevo's abandoned-booking recovery or follow-up features if the plan includes them.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g's long-standing guideline is to avoid new windows and tabs because they disorient users, particularly on mobile. Meevo's docs describe the Google Book Online button, its utm parameters and the 24-72h activation. Zoca identifies the website-to-booking-system handoff as the main blind spot where abandonment goes unmeasured. Zenoti's 2026 benchmark puts abandoned-booking recovery at about $800 per location per month.

recommendations.title: Service menus: prices in full, easy to scan, with jump links
recommendations.detail: Keep every price visible, never behind a 'call for pricing'. Structure: (a) a short intro, (b) a sticky row of jump-link chips at the top on mobile (for example on salon.html: Cuts, Color, Blonding, Extensions, Treatments, Styling), (c) each .menu-group > h3 with .price-item rows (span.name left, span.price right-aligned in tabular numbers, a one-line description below), (d) a small 'Book this' text link per group, deep-linked to Meevo with a utm_content tag. Show ranges as '$37-60' or 'from $37', and add a one-time explainer of the levels ('Price depends on your stylist's level: Jr Associate, Associate, Senior, Expert, Master. More experience, higher price.'). Where the source gives durations (for example massage 30-75 min), show them as '60 min · $XX'. Mark deposits and consult requirements next to the item (Keratin: consultation + $50 deposit). Put a short policies strip (24h notice) near the bottom of each menu, not in a pop-up. Keep the existing markup contract so tools/build-schema.py still produces its JSON-LD.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g: price is users' #1 information need, users go to competitors when prices are hidden, companies that hide costs are seen as evasive, and when an exact price isn't possible, show a range or sample price. NN/g also recommends in-page links at the top of long content on mobile. Salon-industry guides (Zenoti, Booksy) recommend categorized menus, 'from' pricing, and labeling tiers by stylist level. Zoca lists unexpectedly high prices at service selection as a top reason people abandon mid-booking. Showing prices on the site first prevents that surprise.

recommendations.title: A 'New Guests' path (nav item + homepage band)
recommendations.detail: Build a New Guests page or section that answers first-visit worries in order: (1) Not sure who to book? Take the Mya match quiz (https://app.joinmya.com/bellezza) or call and client services will match you. (2) How pricing works (stylist levels). (3) What to expect: arrive 10 minutes early, consultation included, parking at 206 Deo Drive. Confirm every such detail with the salon first, because these are not in the verified facts. (4) Policies in plain language: 24h notice, the no-show escalation, the etiquette. (5) Book online / call / download the app. On the homepage, use a 'Find your Bellezza match' band with one button to the quiz and a secondary 'Book an appointment'. Also link the quiz from our-team.html ('Not sure who to choose?').
recommendations.evidence: Boulevard's retention research, as reported by Salon Today, found first-time clients who book online return for a second visit about 78% of the time vs about 39% for walk-ins. Mya reports one salon getting 514 leads in 90 days and retention rising from 35% to 64%. That is vendor-reported, so treat it as directional. Zenoti found 46% choose a salon on a friend's referral, so first-timers arrive with a name but no idea which provider to pick.

recommendations.title: Live 'Open now' status and complete hours
recommendations.detail: Compute open or closed in site.js using the America/New_York time zone (Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone), not the visitor's clock. Show 'Open now · until 8pm', 'Opens today at 12pm', 'Closed · opens Mon 9am', or on holidays 'Closed today for Labor Day'. Encode the fixed holidays (Jan 1, Jul 4, Dec 25-26), the computed ones (Memorial Day = last Monday of May, Labor Day = first Monday of September), and the early closes (Dec 24 and Dec 31 at 12pm, Jul 3 at 5pm). Put the Trick-or-Treat night date in one clearly marked config entry, since the city sets it each year. Put the status in the utility bar, the hero proof line and the contact/visit block, and pair it with the full weekly table (today's row highlighted). Render the static table in the HTML so it still works without JS. Keep openingHoursSpecification in the JSON-LD in sync, and keep Google Business Profile special hours updated for the same holidays.
recommendations.evidence: Think with Google data cited by several local-SEO sources: 'open now near me' searches grew 400%+ year over year, and 76% of local 'nearby' smartphone searches lead to a same-day visit. Salon Today/Phorest (5,000+ salons, 2019) found 46% of appointments are booked outside opening hours, 28% in the evening and 18% before opening. So the status should push after-hours visitors to online booking ('Closed now, book online anytime').

recommendations.title: After-hours messaging turns 'closed' into 'book now'
recommendations.detail: When the status is closed, change the call-oriented microcopy to 'We're closed right now. Book online 24/7 or on the Bellezza app.' The mobile bar keeps Book as the primary action at all hours. Only relabel the Call button when closed (for example to 'Call (opens 9am)'); don't remove it.
recommendations.evidence: Phorest data: 46% of salon bookings happen outside business hours. Zenoti 2025 survey: 48% of salon regulars would be 'much more likely' to return if they could book or change appointments anytime, and 55% find limited booking hours frustrating.

recommendations.title: Social proof: verifiable third-party proof, placed where people decide
recommendations.detail: We have no real testimonials yet, so lead with proof we can verify: 'Voted #1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016' (hero proof line and trust bar), 'Est. 2009', '28-person team', the named professional credentials in team bios (schools, years, CNP), and the professional brands carried (Dermalogica, Olaplex, etc.). Once reviews exist, show 2-3 real, attributed Google reviews (first name + last initial, date, service) next to the hero CTA or the final booking band, plus 'Read our reviews on Google' with a link to the Google Business Profile. Don't build the section until then. Link the Meevo Five Star ratings page from the footer or contact page, and after-visit, to collect reviews. No star widgets or counts that aren't real.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g: people trust testimonials from external sites more than ones on the business's own site, and being connected to the rest of the web (reviews, social) is one of 4 credibility factors. BrightLocal 2025 (1,026 US consumers): Google is used by 83-85% of people checking reviews; only 4% never read reviews; the most trusted rating range is 4.2-4.5 stars; consumers increasingly accept businesses with fewer than 50 reviews and reviews 6-12 months old. BrightLocal 2024: 71% won't consider a business under 3 stars.

recommendations.title: Promote gift cards all year, with a seasonal boost
recommendations.detail: Keep 'Gift cards' in the utility bar and footer, plus a slim band on the homepage and at the bottom of the massage, facial and spray-tan pages ('Give a massage: send an eGift card instantly'), linking straight to the Meevo eGift app. On gift-cards.html, say it's delivered instantly by email, suggest amounts tied to real services (for example 'Custom signature facial $90', 'Relaxation massage from $42'), and state the exclusion plainly: 'Not valid at Slay Aesthetics.' Put a date-driven banner in site.js for mid-November through Dec 24 and the week before Mother's Day and Valentine's Day, so the promotion switches on and off without anyone editing pages.
recommendations.evidence: Zenoti's holiday guide: 25% of gift cards are redeemed by new customers, so gift cards also bring in new clients. 75% of recipients spend more than the card's value, and 60% of $100 recipients spend $74+ more (Blackhawk 2022). 80% of US shoppers start holiday buying by November (NRF 2023). Spa-industry sources say gift cards can reach about 22% of revenue at some spas. That figure is from a single vendor, so treat it as directional.

recommendations.title: Tap-to-call and contact details on every page
recommendations.detail: Wrap every phone number in 740-366-1604 and show the digits, not just an icon. Make the address a link to Google Maps directions. Include name, address, phone and hours in the footer of every page (site.js already injects the footer). The bridal email can be shown as text with a mailto link beside it. On the contact page, order it: Call, Get directions, Book online, then the hours table, then the map. Don't lead with a form.
recommendations.evidence: Google/Ipsos: 94% of smartphone users have needed to call a business while searching, 70% have used click-to-call, and 61% say calling matters most at the purchase stage. NN/g credibility research: show contact info, address and phone prominently. web.dev recommends tel: links with international format.

recommendations.title: Forms: as few as possible, short, and forgiving
recommendations.detail: Send booking to Meevo, not to a 'request an appointment' form. Only use forms where needed (bridal inquiry, careers, pick-up orders). Bridal inquiry: name, email, phone, wedding date, party size and services (checkboxes), message (optional). Mark optional fields, not required ones. Use type=email/tel/date, autocomplete attributes, labels above fields (not placeholder-only), and at least 48px input height with 16px text so iOS doesn't zoom. Validate when the visitor leaves a field (not on every keystroke) and show errors inline next to the field. The host is static, so use Netlify Forms (data-netlify="true") or a Cloudflare-compatible endpoint, add a honeypot field, handle submit in JS, and show a clear success state that says who replies and when ('Our bridal coordinator will reply within 2 business days'; confirm that timeframe with the salon).
recommendations.evidence: Baymard: 31% of sites lack live inline validation, validating when the visitor leaves a field reduces errors, and error handling, not field count, is where people give up on forms they meant to finish. Average checkout forms have about 11.3 fields vs an ideal of about 8-12. Industry booking guidance: about 7% more abandonment for each extra required field.

recommendations.title: Tap targets and contrast for CTAs
recommendations.detail: All buttons and nav links need a touch area of at least 44x44px (48px is better on the mobile bar), with at least 8px between adjacent targets. WCAG 2.2 AA requires at least 24x24px. Contrast from the brand palette: ink on gold 6.24:1 (OK for button text), white on gold 2.73:1 (fail), white on gold-dk #9c7f4c 3.78:1 (large or bold text 18.66px+ only), gold #b8985f text on cream #faf8f5 2.57:1 (fail; decoration only, never small labels or links), gold-dk on cream 3.57:1 (large text only), body #6b6b6b on cream 5.03:1 (passes AA; don't go lighter), gold on black 7.69:1 (fine for the top bar and dark booking band). Keep focus rings visible (a 2px ink outline with offset).
recommendations.evidence: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 sets a 24x24 CSS px minimum; Apple recommends 44pt and Material 48dp; NN/g says at least 1cm x 1cm on touchscreens. We computed the contrast ratios with the WCAG relative-luminance formula for the required palette.

recommendations.title: Keep the page fast, because slow pages lose visitors before they book
recommendations.detail: Target LCP under 2.5s on 4G. Serve hero and portraits as AVIF/WebP with srcset/sizes (the 720x960 headshots need 360w and 720w versions). Set width and height to prevent layout shift, fetchpriority="high" on the hero image, loading="lazy" on everything below the fold, and font-display: swap. Preload only the Prata weight used for headings. No map iframe on load: use a static map image or a 'Get directions' button, and load the iframe only on click. The Google Drive promo video should be tap-to-play, never autoplay.
recommendations.evidence: Google/SOASTA (900k mobile landing pages): the chance of a bounce rises 32% as load time goes from 1s to 3s and 90% from 1s to 5s; 53% of mobile visits are abandoned after 3s.

recommendations.title: Put booking next to each provider on the team page
recommendations.detail: On our-team.html, give each card name, role or level, specialties as tags (for example 'Blonding · Extensions'), and 'Book with Austyn'. Link to Meevo; if Meevo supports deep-linking to a provider, use it, otherwise link to the general booking page with utm_content=team-austyn. Keep the dialog.bio contents (school, years, specialties, Instagram link) and put the Book button inside the dialog too. Add filter chips (Hair, Nails, Skin, Massage, Aesthetics, Makeup, Bridal) as progressive enhancement over the static list. Put 'Not sure who? Take the match quiz' above the grid.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g credibility research: showing real staff and specific expertise builds trust. Mya/Zenoti: matching clients to the right provider improves first-visit rebooking. Meevo's public docs don't mention provider deep-links, so confirm with Meevo support before relying on them.

recommendations.title: Measure the funnel
recommendations.detail: Add privacy-light analytics (Plausible, Fathom or GA4) with click events on every outbound Meevo link (data-cta="hero|header|mobilebar|menu-salon|team|quiz|giftcard"), on tel: clicks, and on quiz clicks. Combine these with the UTM tags on Meevo links so Meevo's own reports show which placements produce completed bookings. Review monthly and move or remove placements that don't earn clicks.
recommendations.evidence: Zoca: salons can't see booking abandonment because marketing tools lose track of visitors once they reach third-party booking software, so tagging the handoff is the only way to see the funnel from a static site.

pitfalls: Routing Book buttons through an intermediate book-online.html page instead of straight to Meevo. Every extra step costs bookings.
White text on the gold #b8985f button (2.73:1, fails WCAG AA). Use ink #1c1c1c text on gold, or gold on black.
Using gold #b8985f for small labels, eyebrows or links on cream (2.57:1). It reads as faint, looks like a template, and fails accessibility.
Auto-rotating hero sliders or before/after carousels. NN/g shows users miss the content, and on mobile they have scrolled past before it changes.

Fake or placeholder testimonials, star ratings, review counts or 'as seen in' logos. None exist yet. Made-up proof destroys trust and breaks FTC rules; lead with the verifiable '#1 spa in Licking County since 2016' instead.
'Call for pricing' or hiding prices behind the booking system. NN/g shows users leave for competitors and read it as evasive.
A translucent or blurred sticky header over photos, or a tall header plus a utility bar that both stay pinned and take a third of a phone screen.
A sticky mobile bar that covers footer content or the cookie/consent UI, or stacks on top of another Book band. Add body padding and hide the bar when the final CTA band is visible.
Several competing gold buttons in one view (Book, Gift cards, Quiz, Shop all gold). Gold should mean 'book'.
Vague CTA labels like 'Learn more', 'Click here', 'Submit', or icon-only phone buttons with no number.
Opening Meevo in a new tab without saying so. Mobile users lose the tab and think the site broke.
Pop-up modals (newsletter or promo) on first load. They get in the way of the one job the visitor came to do.
Using the handwritten script font for the headline, prices, CTAs or anything that must be read quickly over a photo.
An 'Open now' badge computed from the visitor's device time zone, or one that ignores the holiday and early-close schedule, which sends people to a closed salon.
Contact forms as a stand-in for booking ('request an appointment'). They add delay and staff follow-up, and clients now expect instant self-booking.
Lazy-loading or poorly compressing the hero image, loading map iframes and Drive video embeds on page load. This hurts mobile LCP and bounce rate.
bellezza_specific: Centralize CTA URLs in the existing site.js config object (booking, tel, giftcards, ratings) and add quiz: 'https://app.joinmya.com/bellezza'. Add a helper that appends utm_source=website&utm_medium=cta&utm_content=<placement> to every [data-book] link, and test once that Meevo accepts the extra query parameters.

Change the nav's 'Book Online' (currently book-online.html) to a gold 'Book now' button linking straight to Meevo. Keep book-online.html as an explainer page (the app badges, what to expect, the 24h policy, the phone number) linked from New Guests and the footer.

Hero proof line: 'Voted #1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016 · Newark since 2009 · 28 beauty professionals'. Every part is verified; don't use the mockup's '20+'. Use the exact count or 'more than 25'.

Mobile bottom bar on every page: [Book an appointment] gold with ink text + [Call] linked to tel:+17403661604; add padding-bottom: calc(64px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) to body and hide the bar when the dark 'Book your appointment today' band is in view.

Hours logic in site.js with America/New_York: Mon-Tue 9-8, Wed 12-8, Thu 9-8, Fri 9-7, Sat 8-3, Sun closed; closed Jan 1, Memorial Day (last Mon in May), Jul 4, Labor Day (1st Mon in Sep), Dec 25-26; close at 12pm Dec 24 and 31; close at 5pm Jul 3; put Newark Trick-or-Treat night as a yearly config date. Wednesday opening at noon is unusual, so the live status line saves wasted calls.

Service pages: add sticky jump-link chips at the top (for example tips-and-toes: Manicures, Pedicures, Gel, Enhancements, Add-ons, using the actual h3 group names). Put a one-time level explainer under the intro ('Prices vary by artist level: Associate / Senior / Expert'), show prices in tabular numbers, and put a 'Book this' link after each .menu-group. Keep .menu-group > h3 / .price-item span.name/span.price + following p intact for tools/build-schema.py.
Put the Keratin '$50 deposit + consultation required' and the Slay Aesthetics 'Bellezza gift cards not accepted' notes right next to the relevant items and on gift-cards.html, not only in policies.

New Guests nav item (from the mockup) → a page with: match quiz (Mya) → how pricing and levels work → policies in plain words (24h notice; the no-show steps: reminder, then 50% deposit, then 100% prepayment; etiquette) → Book / Call / app badges. Don't invent 'arrive 10 minutes early' or parking details; confirm them with the salon first.

Bridal: primary CTA 'Plan your bridal beauty' goes to an inquiry form (static-host form) plus the visible email dsabo@bellezzaspaonline.com. Mention the travel team 'available for a fee' and name Devon (bridal lead). Secondary CTA: book a trial via Meevo.

Gift cards: link to the utility-bar 'Gift cards', a homepage band, and the bottom of the massage/facial/spray-tan pages. Seasonal banner auto-on mid-Nov to Dec 24, and in the 10 days before Valentine's Day and Mother's Day. Suggest amounts tied to real prices (facial $90, massage from $42, spray tan $35).

Team page: 'Book with <name>' in each card and in each dialog.bio. Add filter chips by discipline and a 'Not sure who? Find your match' link to the quiz above the grid. Show levels (Jr Associate → Master) as tags, since they explain the price differences.

Reviews: we have none, so don't build a testimonial section yet. Link the Meevo Five Star ratings page and the Google Business Profile. Once real Google reviews exist, feature 2-3 with first name + initial, service and date near the final CTA band.

Turn on Meevo's Google Book Online button (MeevoXchange > Integrations; the name and address must exactly match the Google profile: 'Bellezza & Co.', 206 Deo Drive, Newark, OH 43055) so Google Search and Maps visitors can book without going through the website.

Contact/visit block order: 'Open now · until 8pm' → Call 740-366-1604 → Get directions (Google Maps link to 206 Deo Drive) → Book online → hours table with today highlighted → a map image that loads the interactive map on click (no storefront photo exists, so use the map or the team group photo join-1.jpg).

dimension: Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and Performance (Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP, CLS) for the Bellezza static rebuild

recommendations.title: Add accessible gold variants and assign every color a role (contrast ratios computed)
recommendations.detail:
Ratios computed with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula. Pass levels: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (24px+, or 18.66px+ bold) and for UI parts/focus rings.

WHAT PASSES AND WHAT FAILS
- gold #b8985f on #fff: 2.73. Fails everything, including large text and UI.
- gold #b8985f on #faf8f5: 2.57. Fails everything.
- gold #b8985f on #1c1c1c: 6.24. Passes normal text. (On #000: 7.69, also passes.)
- gold-dk #9c7f4c on #fff: 3.78. Large text and UI only; fails normal text.
- gold-dk #9c7f4c on #faf8f5: 3.57. Large text and UI only.
- body #6b6b6b on #fff: 5.33. Passes.
- body #6b6b6b on #faf8f5: 5.03. Passes.
- body #6b6b6b on line #e7e2d9: 4.13. Fails normal text.
- #8a8a8a on #fff: 3.45. Large text only. (On #faf8f5: 3.26.)
- white on #b8985f: 2.73. Fails everything, so the current .btn (white text on gold) fails.
- white on #9c7f4c: 3.78. Large text only, so the current hover state fails for button text.
- #1c1c1c on #b8985f: 6.24. Passes normal text.
- #1c1c1c on #9c7f4c: 4.51. Passes, but only just.
- line #e7e2d9 on #fff: 1.29. Fails the 3:1 UI requirement as an input border.

NEW TOKENS (same hue as the existing gold, about 38 degrees, only darker or lighter)
```css
:root{
  --gold:#b8985f;      /* brand: fills, rules, ornaments, text on dark */
  --gold-dk:#9c7f4c;   /* borders, icons, focus rings, 24px+ display text on light */
  --gold-text:#846a3b; /* small gold text on light: 5.11 on #fff, 4.82 on #faf8f5; white on it 5.11 */
  --gold-deep:#6a552f; /* hover/pressed: 7.11 on #fff */
  --gold-lt:#c9ae7c;   /* hover fill behind ink text: 7.98 with #1c1c1c */
  --ink:#1c1c1c; --body:#6b6b6b; --line:#e7e2d9; --alt:#faf8f5;
  --field-border:#9c7f4c; /* 3.78 on white, meets 1.4.11 */
}
```
The lightest same-hue gold that passes 4.5 is #8f723f on white and #8a6e3d on cream. #846a3b adds a safety margin.

BUTTON RECOMMENDATION (keeps the signature gold fill)
```css

recommendations.title: Move the header, nav and footer into static HTML instead of injecting them with JS
recommendations.detail:
Today site.js runs `fill()` on DOMContentLoaded and replaces empty `<div id="site-topbar">`, `<div id="site-header">` and `<div id="site-footer">` with markup.

Problems this causes:
- CLS: the header (about 100 to 150px) pushes all content down after first paint. This is likely the single largest CLS source on every page.
- LCP: the LCP element can render and then get shoved, which delays the final render.
- Crawlability: the nav links and the NAP (name, address, phone) in the footer are not in the raw HTML. Google renders JS, but other crawlers, AI assistants and link-preview bots do not.
- No-JS: with JS off, there is no navigation at all.

Fix without adding a serve-time build step:
1. Add `tools/build-partials.py`, modeled on build-schema.py.
2. It reads `partials/header.html` and `partials/footer.html` and stamps them between markers in every page, for example `<!-- partial:header:start -->` ... `<!-- partial:header:end -->`.
3. It sets `aria-current="page"` on the matching nav link per file.
4. site.js then only adds behavior (menu toggle, dialogs, year). It never injects layout.
5. Keep the phone, the Book link and the address in the same header and footer spot on every page.

If the owner insists on JS includes as a stopgap, reserve the space (`#site-header{min-height:var(--header-h)}`), load site.js with `defer`, and inject synchronously before first paint. Static markup is far better.
recommendations.evidence: web.dev (Optimize CLS): reserve space for late-injected content and avoid inserting content above existing content. web.dev (Optimize LCP): server-rendered HTML makes resources discoverable and avoids render delay. Google Search Central: injected links are fine if they are `<a href>`, but 'server-side or pre-rendering is still a great idea because it makes your website faster for users and crawlers, and not all bots can run JavaScript.' WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 Consistent Help (A) requires help mechanisms such as a phone number or contact link to appear in the same relative place on every page.

recommendations.title: Make the hero image load first: an in the HTML, never lazy-loaded
recommendations.detail: The hero photo will be the LCP element on the home page. Put it in the HTML as a real ``, not a CSS background and not inserted by JS: ```html ``` Rules: - Use `fetchpriority="high"` on this one image only. - No `loading="lazy"` on anything above the fold. - The current hero carousel: if kept, only slide 1 gets high priority and the other slides get `fetchpriority="low" loading="lazy"`. - Interior page banners (`.page-banner` currently uses a CSS background): convert to an `` with `object-fit:cover`, or add `` in ``.
recommendations.evidence: web.dev (Optimize LCP): 'Never lazy-load your LCP image'; avoid injecting images via JS or data-src; limit high priority to one or two resources; the target is LCP of 2.5s or less at p75. web.dev (Fetch Priority): cites Google Flights LCP dropping from 2.6s to 1.9s with fetchpriority=high; for CSS background images, 'Preload is still required' with fetchpriority=high on the preload.

recommendations.title: Responsive image pipeline: AVIF/WebP/JPEG at several widths, width/height on every image
recommendations.detail: assets/img is 8.7 MB, all JPG/PNG, with 0 WebP and 0 AVIF files. Pillow 12.2 is installed locally and can write both formats. Add `tools/build-images.py`, a one-time offline script like build-schema.py, so the site still needs no build step to serve. It should: - Write `name-{w}.avif`, `name-{w}.webp` and `name-{w}.jpg` at 400, 800, 1200 and 1600 widths for photos. Use 360, 540 and 720 widths for the 720x960 headshots. - Use quality of about 50 for AVIF, 75 for WebP and 78 (progressive) for JPEG. - Strip EXIF, which matters for staff photos. Markup rules: - Every `` gets intrinsic `width` and `height`, plus `img{max-width:100%;height:auto}`. - Cropped tiles use CSS `aspect-ratio` with `object-fit:cover`. - Below-the-fold images get `loading="lazy" decoding="async"`. - `sizes` must match the layout. Examples: 4-up team grid `sizes="(min-width:1100px) 260px, (min-width:700px) 45vw, 90vw"`; 6-tile services mosaic `sizes="(min-width:900px) 33vw, 50vw"`. Fixes in the current markup: - Dialog bio images have no width/height: add `width="720" height="960"`. - Logos and brand PNGs should become SVG or WebP. - The black logo PNG (786x257) needs a white variant for the dark footer band.
recommendations.evidence: web.dev Learn Images: srcset `w` descriptors plus `sizes` let the browser choose the right file. web.dev (Optimize CLS): always include width/height; browsers derive aspect ratio from them. web.dev (Optimize LCP): modern formats and responsive sizing cut resource load duration.

recommendations.title: Fix font loading: remove the CSS @import, self-host WOFF2, fewer weights, metric-matched fallbacks
recommendations.evidence: Tune The Web (Barry Pollard): self-hosting cut the Web Almanac's load time from 6s to 3s. Cache partitioning removed the shared-CDN cache benefit, and Google Fonts CSS blocks rendering across two extra origins. Recommended steps there: WOFF2 only, subset, unicode-range, font-display swap, preload judiciously. Chrome Developers (font fallbacks): size-adjust and the ascent, descent and line-gap overrides stop swap-induced layout shift. web.dev (Optimize CLS) recommends the same. Fetching the Prata ital@1 CSS confirmed no italic face exists.

recommendations.title: Visible focus styles with :focus-visible, and focus that sticky bars cannot hide
recommendations.evidence: MDN: :focus-visible shows the ring for keyboard use and not for mouse clicks; inputs always match; the ring needs 3:1 contrast (1.4.11). WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA): a focused component may not be entirely hidden by author content such as sticky headers or footers; the recommended technique is CSS scroll-padding. 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA) sets a 3:1, 2px-perimeter benchmark worth meeting.

recommendations.title: Hero and 'Transformations' carousel: no autoplay, or add a real pause control; offer a keyboard alternative to dragging

For the redesign: - Use a single static hero photo. That is better for both LCP and accessibility. - For the before/after section, use a user-driven, scroll-snap row with prev/next `
recommendations.evidence: WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide: content that auto-advances for more than 5 seconds alongside other content needs pause, stop or hide controls. recommendations.title: Respect reduced motion
recommendations.evidence: MDN prefers-reduced-motion: tone down scaling and panning motion and swap in opacity changes for users with vestibular disorders; widely supported since 2020. web.dev (Optimize CLS): animate composited properties (transform) to avoid layout shifts.

recommendations.title: Team bio dialogs: native <dialog> done right (keep dialog.bio for build-schema.py)

recommendations.title: Navigation: use the disclosure pattern, not role=menu, and fix how the mobile parent link behaves
recommendations.detail:
Current mobile behavior intercepts the tap on parent links such as 'Services' (`e.preventDefault()`), so the Services landing page cannot be reached on phones, and screen readers hear a link that does not navigate. Use a link and a separate toggle button: ```html
  • Services
      ...
    • ``` - Esc closes an open submenu and returns focus to its toggle. - On desktop, open on `:hover` and `:focus-within` as a progressive enhancement, but the button must work too. - The mobile menu button needs `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls="primary-nav"`. It already has aria-expanded. - Use `aria-current="page"`, stamped by build-partials.py, instead of only the `.is-active` class. - Do not use role=menu or menubar. - Keep the header nav short (Services, Meet the Team, New Guests, Bridal, About) plus a persistent Book Now button that is always visible, never inside the collapsed menu.
recommendations.evidence: W3C WAI-ARIA APG disclosure navigation example: buttons use aria-expanded and aria-controls; links use aria-current="page"; Esc closes; 'does not use the WAI-ARIA menu role' because site navigation lacks menu-widget keyboard semantics.

recommendations.title: Accordions (FAQ, policies, service details) with <details name>
recommendations.detail:
Use native disclosure elements for the policies, New Guests FAQ, and the 'what's included' notes under services: ```html

``` - Keep the exact existing structure of `.menu-group > h3` / `.price-item` in the price lists. Do not collapse price lists into accordions, because build-schema.py parses them. - Hidden price information also hurts scanning and click intent. - Style it with `summary{list-style:none;min-height:48px;display:flex;align-items:center;cursor:pointer}` and `summary::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}`, plus a rotating chevron in `summary::after` using transform. - A shared `name` makes an exclusive group; skip it if users might want several items open at once. - If schema FAQPage is desired, the text must match what is visible.

recommendations.title: Keep INP low: small deferred JS, facades for heavy third parties
recommendations.detail:
Scripts:
- Load `<script src="assets/js/site.js" defer>`. It is currently at the end of body with no defer, which is fine, but defer in the head is cleaner once no layout is injected.
- Use event delegation, and do no layout reads and writes in the same handler.

Third parties (the main INP risk on a site like this):
- Do not embed the Meevo booking page, the Mya quiz or Instagram feeds in iframes on content pages. Link out with clear buttons instead. The Book CTA can open Meevo in the same tab so the back button works.
- For the map, show a static map image (a self-made screenshot or illustration) that links to Google Maps directions. Do not use an iframe at load. If an iframe is required, use a click-to-load facade with `loading="lazy"`.
- Promo video: a poster image with a play button that links to or loads the video on click.

Other:
- Long pages such as our-team (28 cards) and price menus: `section{content-visibility:auto;contain-intrinsic-size:auto 800px}` on below-fold sections cuts rendering work.
- Optional progressive enhancement for instant page-to-page navigation in Chromium: `<script type="speculationrules">{"prerender":[{"where":{"href_matches":"/*"},"eagerness":"moderate"}]}</script>`.
- Do not add `unload` handlers or `Cache-Control: no-store` on HTML. Both block the back/forward cache.
recommendations.evidence: web.dev (Optimize INP): target 200ms or less at p75; minimize main-thread work; avoid long tasks and layout thrashing; content-visibility reduces rendering work; avoid rendering large HTML via JS in response to interactions. web.dev (Optimize CLS): back/forward cache eligibility removes shifts on return navigations.

recommendations.title: Mobile sticky 'Book' bar that respects safe areas and focus visibility
recommendations.evidence: WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: sticky elements must not fully cover focused items; the scroll-padding technique handles this. WCAG 2.5.8 covers target size. The prior design notes also flagged that the page is long on phones and the Book button should stay visible.

recommendations.title: Text readability: sizes, weights, script overlays, alt text
recommendations.detail:
Sizes and weights:
- Body text: 17 to 18px, weight 400, line-height 1.6, max-width about 68ch.
- Microtype such as eyebrows and button labels (currently .72 to .78rem with 0.22 to 0.3em letter-spacing): use at least 13px (0.8125rem), weight 600, and reduce tracking to about 0.12em.

Script accents:
- Handwritten accents like 'Good Hair Brighter Days' are decorative. Put them in `aria-hidden="true"` elements, never over busy photo areas.
- If one carries meaning, add the same words in visually hidden text.
- Place gold script only on the dark band (6.24) or as large text on cream using --gold-dk (3.57, large text only).

Alt text:
- Staff portraits: 'Devon, Salon Manager', not 'image1'.
- Decorative flourishes: alt="".
- The brow before/after graphic needs alt describing both states.

Reflow:
- Test at 320px width and 200% zoom (1.4.10 and 1.4.4).
- Test with the text-spacing bookmarklet (1.4.12). Avoid fixed heights on text containers.
recommendations.evidence: WCAG 1.4.3 (contrast), 1.4.4 (resize), 1.4.10 (reflow), 1.4.12 (text spacing) and 1.1.1 (non-text content). The prior design notes flagged the faint light-grey text and small caps, and hard-to-read script over busy photos.

recommendations.title: Caching headers for a no-build static host
recommendations.detail:
The project already uses `_redirects`, so it is on Netlify or Cloudflare Pages. Add a `_headers` file:
```
/assets/img/*
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
/assets/fonts/*
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
/assets/css/*
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, stale-while-revalidate=86400
/assets/js/*
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, stale-while-revalidate=86400
```
- Treat the image and font files as immutable: when one changes, give it a new filename (for example `-v2`).
- Version CSS and JS with a query string (`styles.css?v=20261001`) stamped by the same Python tool.
- HTML keeps the host default (revalidate).
- Budget: total home-page weight under about 1 MB on mobile; hero image under about 150 KB as AVIF; one CSS file under about 30 KB; JS under about 15 KB.
recommendations.evidence: web.dev (Optimize LCP): efficient cache-control policies make repeat visits load from cache and shorten resource load duration.

pitfalls: White text on the brand gold #b8985f (2.73:1) and gold text on white or cream (2.57 to 2.73:1): both fail even the large-text threshold. This is the most common 'luxury salon template' accessibility failure.
Thin 300-weight grey body text and tiny, widely letter-spaced uppercase labels. They look 'elegant' in a mockup but are unreadable on phones in daylight.
Injecting the header, nav and footer with JS into empty divs. It causes layout shift on every page, hides NAP and nav links from non-JS crawlers, and leaves no navigation without JS.
Lazy-loading the hero image, or making it a CSS background or JS carousel slide. Each delays LCP. Use fetchpriority=high on only one image.
Loading Google Fonts via @import inside the stylesheet. It is the slowest possible chain. Also avoid faux italic Prata (the font has no italic).
Auto-rotating hero or testimonial carousels with no pause control (fails WCAG 2.2.2). Carousels also hide content and are rarely clicked past slide 1.
Before/after sliders that only work by dragging (fails 2.5.7). Use a native range input.
Removing outlines (outline:none) or 1px low-contrast focus rings. Also, sticky headers and bottom Book bars that cover the focused element without scroll-padding.
Parent nav links hijacked with preventDefault on mobile, and using role=menu for site navigation.
Input borders in the #e7e2d9 line color (1.29:1). Form fields need boundaries of at least 3:1.
Links in body copy distinguished only by gold color. Underline them.
Embedding Instagram feeds, Google Maps iframes, the Meevo booking iframe or the Mya quiz on page load. These are heavy third-party scripts that hurt INP and LCP. Use links or click-to-load facades.
Missing width/height on images, including the dialog bio images and new mosaic tiles, which causes CLS.
Decorative script overlays on busy photos, and meaningful text baked into images such as the specials promo graphics with no text equivalent.
Collapsing price lists into accordions or restructuring them in ways that break tools/build-schema.py (.menu-group > h3, .price-item span.name/span.price, .card, dialog.bio, article.job).

recommendations.title: Design at phone width first (360 to 430px), then scale up
recommendations.detail: Build every section at 360px wide first, then adapt at 768px and 1100px or wider. At phone width the hero shows, in this order: headline, one line of intro copy, a Book an Appointment button (gold with ink text), an Explore Services link, and a one-line proof strip ('Voted #1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016 · Est. 2009'). recommendations.title: Header: a combined nav pattern (a few visible links plus a menu), with a labeled 'Menu' button on phones
recommendations.detail: Desktop (1100px and up): logo on the left. Visible text nav: Services (dropdown), Bridal, Our Team, New Guests, About, Gift Cards. A gold 'Book Now' button with ink text on the right. Never use a hamburger on desktop. Phones: logo on the left, then a small 'Book' button, then a hamburger with the visible word 'Menu' under or beside it, on the right. The header is opaque cream (#faf8f5) with a 1px #e7e2d9 bottom border and is 56 to 64px tall. It hides when the user scrolls down and comes back on scroll up (300 to 400ms transition, a few pixels of hysteresis). On phones the black utility bar (address, phone, gift cards, socials) collapses to one line, e.g. 'Open today until 8pm · 740-366-1604', or drops away entirely, because the bottom action bar covers call and directions. The menu drawer, top to bottom: Book online (primary), Call. The 10 service links, visible and not nested in a sub-accordion. Bridal, New Guests, Our Team, About, Specials, Gift Cards, Shop & Pick-up, Careers, Contact. Hours and address at the bottom. The drawer traps focus, closes on Esc, and has aria-expanded on the toggle.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g hidden-vs-visible navigation study: hidden nav cut discoverability by more than 20%. Tasks were 15% slower on mobile and at least 39% slower on desktop, and felt 21% harder. On mobile, combo nav was used 86% of the time against 57% for a hamburger alone. The recommendation is to show visibly when there are 4 or fewer links and never hide nav on desktop. NN/g says label the icon 'Menu'. NN/g sticky headers: make them partially persistent, opaque, and minimal in height.

recommendations.title: Sticky bottom action bar on phones: Call · Directions · Book
recommendations.detail: Below 768px, fix a bar to the bottom with three labeled actions (icon plus text). Call goes to tel:+17403661604. Directions goes to https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=206+Deo+Drive+Newark+OH+43055. Book goes to the Meevo URL and is the widest cell, gold (#b8985f) with ink (#1c1c1c) text. The bar is 56 to 64px tall plus padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom). The site head already sets viewport-fit=cover. Use an opaque cream or ink background with a hairline top border. Add body padding-bottom equal to the bar height so it never covers footer content. Hide the bar while the mobile menu drawer or a bio dialog is open. It is the only persistent element; there is no chat bubble or pop-up on top of it. Keep it to three items: more than that turns it into navigation and shrinks the targets. Tag each action with a data-attribute for analytics events (call_click, directions_click, book_click).
recommendations.evidence: Hoober's field study found 49% of users hold the phone one-handed and 75% of interactions are thumb-driven; the bottom edge suits primary actions and the center suits content. GBP data shows calls and direction requests are core local actions (one benchmark: 21% calls, 9% directions). Google allows small banners that 'take up only a small fraction of the screen' and penalizes full-page interstitials. Sticky CTA tests are mixed (only about a quarter of 33 sticky-element tests won, and product-detail pages did best), so keep the bar small and task-focused and measure it.

recommendations.title: Service taxonomy: 10 pages grouped into 4 families, never more than 2 levels deep
recommendations.detail: Keep the 10 existing URLs so existing links and SEO are preserved; only the visible labels and grouping change. HAIR: Salon (label 'Hair'), Men's Care.
