recommendations.title: Price menus on phones: sticky 'On this page' chips, compact level ladders, accordions only on the longest page
recommendations.detail: Current load: salon.html has 15 groups and 63 rows, because each stylist level is its own row. Tips & Toes has 3 groups and 26 items, Massages 6 and 20. The others have 1 to 3 groups. The pattern: (1) A page summary block at the top: what the category includes, the 'from' price, a 'Price depends on your provider's level' link, 'Who does this' avatars, and a Book button. (2) A sticky horizontal chip row labeled 'On this page' just under the header. It lists the group h3s and highlights the current section on scroll (IntersectionObserver). Headings get scroll-margin-top equal to header plus chip height so they are never hidden. It overflows sideways with a fade edge, and a trailing 'All sections' chip opens a full list so no group is hidden off-screen. (3) Level ladders: for groups whose price-items are levels (Jr Associate to Master), keep the markup exactly as is (.menu-group > h3, li.price-item > span.name + span.price) so tools/build-schema.py still works. Restyle that ul with a modifier class as a 5-cell grid, with the short level name ('Jr Assoc', 'Assoc', 'Senior', 'Expert', 'Master') above a large price. That shrinks each service from 5 rows to about 1.5. (4) Slash prices ('$31 / 37 / 40'): add a small 'Associate / Senior / Expert' legend at the top of each nail and skin group. Leave the span.price text alone. (5) Only on salon.html, wrap the 8 'Color Services' groups in one native <details class="menu-family"> with the summary 'Color: 8 services, from $70', and do the same for Texture and Treatments. Verify build-schema.py still finds .menu-group inside the wrapper. On pages with 6 groups or fewer, leave everything expanded; no accordions. (6) Keep descriptions visible and short, because they drive the decision. (7) No tabs for price menus.
recommendations.evidence: NN/g accordions on mobile: they give a 'big picture before details' and shorten long pages. Don't pre-expand them. Use sticky accordion headers and clear state, because the drawback is disorientation. NN/g tabs: accordions beat tabs on mobile, and horizontally scrolling tab carousels hide options. NN/g in-page links: label them 'On this page', match link text to heading text exactly, highlight the current section, and keep sticky elements from covering headings. Salon tier-pricing guides say a visible level system reduces price complaints.

recommendations.title: One reusable 'How our levels work' explainer, linked to the team
recommendations.detail: Write one block, rendered by site.js or as a shared snippet: 'Prices are set by your provider's level: Jr Associate, Associate, Senior, Expert, Master. Book the level that fits your budget; every level trains in-house.' Use the in-house training line only if the owners confirm it; the verified fact is a paid training and assisting program. Each level name links to the team page filtered to that level (our-team.html#level-senior). Show it as a collapsible note on every priced service page and in full on New Guests. Don't invent criteria such as years or hours for each level.
recommendations.evidence: J. Joseph and similar salons explain levels on a dedicated page tied to their team and pricing: 'the level tells you... how much experience sits behind the chair, and what your service will cost.' Tier guides say a visible level logic reduces pricing complaints and lets budget-minded clients choose.

recommendations.detail: There are 28 cards now. Add a second optional row for hair levels. Filter by data-specialty and data-level attributes on each existing .card, and keep dialog.bio unchanged. Phorest, GlossGenius and Salon Business stylist-bio guidance: list which services each person does, keep bios skimmable at 100 to 200 words, and put a booking link on each profile. Google E-E-A-T: show who does the work and their qualifications.

Examples: facials show Emma and Mia. Massage shows Jesyca, with the Hocking College 2015 degree. Nails show Stephanie, Paige, Madison, Shelbi, Raegan, Rissa, Hope and Emma. recommendations.title: Trust signals: typographic proof strip with verified facts only; send people to Google for reviews

Style the award as a clean typographic mark (gold hairline rule, Prata numerals), not a fake laurel or seal that implies third-party certification. Ask the owners who runs the vote (a newspaper's readers' choice, for example); naming the publication makes the claim much stronger and more verifiable. There are no reviews yet, so don't show a star rating or a count. Add a 'See what clients say on Google' link to the Google Business Profile. recommendations.evidence: BrightLocal 2025/2026: about 97% read reviews, Google is the dominant review source (71 to 85%), 47% won't use a business with fewer than 20 reviews, and 31% require 4.5+ stars. That means proof lives on Google and the site should hand people off to it. Google: LocalBusiness or Organization pages that mark up reviews about themselves (including embedded Google or Facebook widgets) are ineligible for review stars. Baymard: users judge trust by gut feeling and visual cues, but badges work as a 'placebo'. The honest, specific wording matters more than seal graphics.

recommendations.evidence: NN/g: 74% of viewing time goes to the first two screenfuls and attention drops sharply after the fold, so booking and category access belong at the top. Avoid 'false floors' with signifiers that invite scrolling. NN/g carousels: no auto-advance on mobile, 5 frames at most, dots are a poor cue on mobile.

recommendations.title: Live 'Open now' hours with the real holiday closures

recommendations.title: Footer: a readable fat footer, not collapsed accordions

Footers should carry utility links (address, phone, policies), but only important, discoverable content. NN/g About Us: the footer is an essential fallback for About and contact links.

recommendations.title: Touch targets, readability and contrast inside the fixed palette
recommendations.detail: Targets are at least 44x44px (Apple 44pt, Material 48dp; WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 AA minimum is 24px). Chips are 40px tall with 8px gaps. Measured contrast: body #6b6b6b on cream #faf8f5 is 5.03:1, a pass. Gold #b8985f with white text is only 2.73:1, a fail, so gold buttons must use ink #1c1c1c text (6.24:1). Gold-dk #9c7f4c on white is 3.78:1, so use it only for large text (24px+ or 18.66px bold) or decorative rules, never for small caps labels. Small labels use ink or #6b6b6b. Tiny uppercase letter-spaced eyebrow text needs at least 12px, weight 600 and ink color. The script accent font is decorative only: put it on plain backgrounds and never use it for information. Center-screen content can use smaller targets; corner controls (menu, close) need bigger hit areas of about 12mm.
recommendations.evidence: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 and platform HIGs. Hoober: center taps are accurate at about 7mm, corners need about 12mm. The contrast ratios were computed for the actual palette hex values.

recommendations.title: Booking handoff and measurement
recommendations.detail: The site can't make the Meevo flow shorter, so reduce the steps before it. Every Book CTA links straight to https://login.meevo.com/bellezza/ob?locationId=103245. Tell people on the button or with a subtle icon that it opens the booking site. Offer 'Book by phone' next to it for people who prefer calling. Track outbound clicks for Book, Call, Directions, Quiz, Gift card and App badges with a lightweight privacy-friendly analytics tool (Plausible, Cloudflare Web Analytics or Netlify), so the redesign's click-through can be compared before and after. Only show a Smart App Banner (the apple-itunes-app meta tag) if the owners supply the real App Store ID; it is the Google-sanctioned non-intrusive app promotion.
recommendations.evidence: Salon conversion guides call seamless booking the #1 driver, and every extra step costs completions. Google names browser app banners as acceptable, unlike interstitials. Sticky and CTA effects vary by site, so measure them.

recommendations.title: Mobile performance budget
recommendations.detail: Aim for a hero LCP image of 120KB or less as AVIF/WebP with srcset (480/800/1200w), fetchpriority="high" and explicit width and height. Lazy-load everything below the fold. Don't embed a Google Maps iframe on the homepage: use the address card plus a Directions button, and on contact-us load the iframe lazily or behind a click. Self-host or preconnect the fonts, subset Prata, and use font-display: swap. The 28 headshots at 720x960 need a 360w variant for the 2-column phone grid.
recommendations.evidence: Boulevard and GlossGenius: compress images and prioritize mobile speed for booking conversion. NN/g: a heavy first view reduces the attention available for the content that matters.

pitfalls: Hamburger-only navigation on desktop, or an unlabeled icon on mobile. NN/g measured more than 20% lower discoverability and slower tasks.

Fake laurel or seal badges for 'Voted #1'. They read as template filler; a named source in plain typography is stronger.
White text on gold buttons (2.73:1 fails WCAG), and gold-dk small text (3.78:1 fails).
Pre-expanded or nested accordions, and accordions on short price pages. Tabs for price menus, and horizontally scrolling chip or tab rows with no 'All sections' fallback.
A sticky 'On this page' bar that covers section headings (set scroll-margin-top), or a bottom bar that covers the footer or the iOS home indicator (use env(safe-area-inset-bottom) plus body padding).

Stock photos of cotton, candles or lilies as hero or tiles. NN/g found users distrust stock imagery; real team photos are the brand's strongest asset.
Renaming or moving the 10 service URLs. Change labels, not slugs, to keep rankings and inbound links.

Changing the price markup in a way that breaks tools/build-schema.py (.menu-group > h3, .price-item with span.name/span.price and a following p, .card with dialog.bio, article.job). Restyle with CSS modifier classes instead.
Fake per-stylist or per-service Meevo deep links. No verified parameter exists; use the single booking URL.
Thin brand pages that repeat manufacturer copy, and a jobs form still on a 'REPLACE-ME' provider.
Stating unverified specifics (parking, level criteria, response times, award publisher) as fact.
Tiny letter-spaced small-caps grey labels, and script overlays on busy photos, which are unreadable on phones.

recommendations.detail: Give each team card these verifiable fields: name, level and role (Jr Associate, Associate, Senior, Expert or Master), specialties, training with school and year (for example 'C-TEC, 2021', 'Hocking College massage therapy degree, 2015', 'American School of Hair Design, 2002'), years of experience or year joined, and an Instagram link that works as a live portfolio. Explain the level system once, with how price tiers map to levels, and link that explanation from every price list, since clients see 'Associate/Senior/Expert' prices there. On each service page, show the team members who do that service, and link each card back to the service page. Keep the existing #ids so the Person @ids in build-schema.py still resolve. Add alumniOf and knowsAbout to the Person schema only where the fact appears on the page. Only claim 'licensed' or name a state board if the owners confirm it for each person.
recommendations.evidence: From the Quality Rater Guidelines, section 5.6: 'E-E-A-T assessments should be based on the MC itself, the information you find during reputation research, verifiable credentials, etc, not just website or content creator claims of "I'm an expert!"' Overstated claims get a Low rating. Section 3.4 gives a salon example directly: 'you may be able to tell that someone is an expert in hair styling by watching a video of them in action (styling someone's hair) and reading others' comments.'

recommendations.title: Hold Slay Aesthetics to YMYL (medical) standards
recommendations.detail: On the Slay page, name the provider and her credential: 'Shannon Francis, CNP, Certified Nurse Practitioner'. State plainly that Slay Aesthetics is an independent medical aesthetics practice working inside Bellezza on Fridays 10 to 6, that Bellezza staff do not perform injectables or weight-loss treatment, that treatment starts with a consultation, and that Bellezza gift cards aren't accepted there. Link to Slay's own site. Don't promise results or use before/after photos unless they're real and consented. Keep the MedicalBusiness node separate from the salon entity, as build-schema.py already does. Give Slay's services, contact and booking their own clear section so it doesn't read like a Bellezza service.
recommendations.evidence: Google's helpful content guidance gives E-E-A-T extra weight on 'Your Money or Your Life' topics that affect health. The Quality Rater Guidelines say pages on YMYL topics 'should receive a Low rating if there is an unsatisfying amount of information about who is responsible for the website or who created the content'. Botox, fillers and medication-assisted weight loss are health topics.

recommendations.title: Make every claim verifiable, including the award and the team size
recommendations.detail: 'Voted the Number 1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016' is the strongest trust claim on the site. Name who ran the vote and, if possible, link to the results. Until the owners confirm the source, use their exact wording and don't design badges with invented logos or years. For the mockup's '20+ beauty professionals', the facts support '22 stylists, nail artists, skin and massage therapists' (28 people counting managers and client services). Use exact numbers and keep them in sync with the team page. Remove © 2024 and any hard-coded year that can go stale. Generate the year at build time, or leave it off.
recommendations.evidence: From the Quality Rater Guidelines, section 5.6: 'claims of personal experience or expertise that seem overstated or included just to impress website visitors' get a Low rating, and deceptive information about a website is a strong reason for Lowest. Google's title-link documentation lists 'obsolete dates' as a trigger for rewriting titles.

recommendations.title: Show reviews in a way that complies with the FTC rule (16 CFR Part 465, in effect since Oct 21, 2024)
recommendations.detail:
Never publish placeholder or AI-written testimonials. That includes the mockup's Emily R., Jessica M. and Caitlin B. Leave the 'Real people. Real experiences.' band out until you have real reviews. When you do:
- Quote only real client reviews, word for word or trimmed with an ellipsis. Attribute each one: first name and last initial, the platform (Google, Facebook, Meevo), the month and year, and the service.
- Get permission for anything that isn't already public.
- A curated band is fine as long as you label it as a selection and add a prominent 'Read all our Google reviews' link to the full, unfiltered profile. Don't suggest the displayed reviews are all of them.
- If a staff member or family member posts a review, they must clearly disclose the connection.
- Ask every client for reviews, not only happy ones. Never tie a reward to a positive review.
- For Google specifically, don't offer any incentive at all.
- Never threaten or pressure anyone to remove a negative review.
- Don't buy followers or engagement.
- Check that the Meevo Five Star ratings flow doesn't route only happy clients to Google (review gating).
recommendations.evidence: The FTC rule bans fake reviews, including 'AI-generated fake reviews'; compensation 'conditioned on the writing of consumer reviews expressing a particular sentiment'; undisclosed insider reviews; review suppression through 'unfounded or groundless legal threats... intimidation'; and fake social media indicators. The FTC's Q&A says 'organizing reviews in a way that makes it difficult for consumers to know about or find negative reviews could be an unfair or deceptive act.' Generalized requests to all customers are allowed. Courts can impose civil penalties for knowing violations, currently more than $50,000 per violation with annual inflation adjustment.

recommendations.title: Don't put self-serving review stars in the structured data
recommendations.detail: Don't add aggregateRating or Review to the LocalBusiness JSON-LD. build-schema.py correctly leaves them out today, so keep it that way. If a Google or Facebook review widget is ever embedded, it still can't earn stars. Put the effort into Google Business Profile reviews instead, since those drive the local pack.
recommendations.evidence: Google's review snippet documentation: 'If the entity that's being reviewed controls the reviews about itself, their pages that use LocalBusiness or any other type of Organization structured data are ineligible for star review feature.' This applies even to embedded third-party widgets.

recommendations.title: Keep the name, address and phone identical everywhere, and match them to the Google Business Profile
recommendations.detail:
Pick one spelling of each and use it on the site, in the JSON-LD, on the Google Business Profile, Facebook, Instagram, Apple Business Connect, Yelp and the app listings:
- Name: 'Bellezza & Co.'. Mention 'formerly Bellezza Salon and Day Spa' in text and as the schema alternateName.
- Address: '206 Deo Drive, Newark, OH 43055'.
- Phone: '(740) 366-1604'.

Hours must match to the minute, including Wednesday 12 to 8 and Saturday 8 to 3. Before each closure, enter the listed holidays and early closings as Special Hours on the Google Business Profile. Show the same schedule in an 'Upcoming holiday hours' block on Contact and in the footer. Generate matching openingHoursSpecification entries with validFrom/validThrough, and opens and closes both '00:00' for full-day closures, from a holiday table in build-schema.py so everything comes from one source. Make the homepage the Google Business Profile website link. A UTM tag on that link is fine; the canonical stays the clean URL.
recommendations.evidence: In Whitespark's 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors, 'HTML NAP Matching GBP NAP' ranks #15 for the local pack and 'Business Open at Search Time' ranks #5. Google's Business Profile guidelines say the name 'should reflect your business's real-world name, as used consistently on your storefront, website, stationery', and special hours for holidays are supported. Google's LocalBusiness documentation shows validFrom/validThrough and the 00:00/00:00 closed-all-day pattern.

recommendations.title: Put the header, nav, footer and contact details in the HTML itself, not in JavaScript
recommendations.detail: Today site.js injects the top bar, header and footer into placeholder divs, so the address, phone, hours and every nav link only exist after JavaScript runs. Extend the build step (the same way build-schema.py stamps JSON-LD) to write the header and footer partials into each .html file. Keep site.js for behavior only: menu toggle, sticky Book bar, current-page highlighting. This also stops layout shift from late-injected headers.
recommendations.evidence: Vercel's crawler study found 'None of the major AI crawlers currently render JavaScript' (GPTBot, ClaudeBot and others), and BrightLocal 2026 found 45% of consumers now use AI tools for local recommendations. Google's link guidance says it 'can only crawl your link if it's an <a> HTML element with an href attribute', and its AI-features guidance says to make sure 'important content is available in textual form'. CLS must stay at or below 0.1.

recommendations.title: Rewrite title tags as 'Service in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (about 45 to 60 characters)
recommendations.detail:
The current titles start with internal names like 'Tips and Toes' or 'Massages' and mostly leave out the city. Put the searcher's words and the city first and the brand last. Suggested titles, with character counts:
- Home (the Google Business Profile landing page): 'Hair Salon & Day Spa in Newark, Ohio | Bellezza & Co.' (53)
- salon: 'Haircuts, Color & Extensions in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (59)
- tips-and-toes: 'Manicures & Pedicures in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (52)
- massages: 'Massage Therapy in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (46)
- facials: 'Dermalogica Facials in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (50)
- brides: 'Bridal Hair & Makeup in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (51)
- hair-removal: 'Waxing in Newark, OH: Brows to Brazilian | Bellezza & Co.' (57)
- makeup-and-eyes: 'Brows, Lashes & Makeup in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (53)
- spray-tans: 'Custom Spray Tans in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (48)
- mens-care: 'Men's Haircuts & Grooming in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.' (56)
- our-team: 'Meet Our Stylists, Nail Artists & Therapists | Bellezza & Co.'
- slay-aesthetics: 'Botox & Fillers in Newark, OH | Slay Aesthetics at Bellezza'

Make each page's single H1 say the same thing in natural words, for example 'Manicures & Pedicures' with 'Tips & Toes' as an eyebrow label, so Google doesn't rewrite the title. Use each city name once. Don't list nearby towns.
recommendations.evidence: Google's title-link documentation: 'Write descriptive and concise text', avoid 'keyword stuffing' and 'boilerplate', 'include just your site name at the beginning or end... separated... with a delimiter', and make the main title clear, because Google rewrites titles using headings when they don't match. Backlinko (4M results): 'Title tags between 40 to 60 characters have the highest CTR' (+8.9%), and positive-sentiment titles gain about 4.1% absolute CTR. Whitespark 2026: 'Keywords in Landing Page Title' ranks #4 for local organic and 'Keywords in GBP Landing Page Title Tag' ranks #17 for the local pack.

recommendations.title: Write a unique meta description for each page, with a real price, a proof point and a next step
recommendations.detail:
Keep each one to about 140 to 160 characters, in plain sentences, with a concrete hook. Examples:
- Home: 'Voted Licking County's #1 spa every year since 2016. Hair, nails, facials, massage and bridal on Deo Drive in Newark. Open evenings until 8. Book online.'
- salon: 'Women's cuts from $37 and all-over color from $70, plus balayage, keratin and hand-sewn extensions by Newark's Master stylists. See every price, then book online.'
- tips-and-toes: 'Gel manicures from $44, plus dip, Gel X, structure gel and pedicures in Newark, OH. Prices by artist level. Book online any time.'
- massages: 'Relaxation massage from $42, plus deep tissue, hot stone, Ashiatsu and prenatal. Newark's voted-#1 day spa. Book online.'

Have build-schema.py compute each page's lowest price from .price-item span.price and warn when a description quotes a different 'from $X', so snippets never go stale.
recommendations.evidence: Google's snippet documentation: 'Create unique descriptions for each page'; 'it's also a great place to include information about the page'; avoid 'long strings of keywords'; Google may use the meta description 'if it might give users a more accurate description of the page than content taken directly from the page.'

recommendations.title: Keep structured data honest and aimed at features Google actually shows (status as of Sept 2026)
recommendations.detail:
What to keep, change or skip:
- **Keep:** the LocalBusiness @type array (DaySpa, HairSalon, NailSalon) with name, address, telephone, url, geo (5 or more decimals), openingHoursSpecification, priceRange under 100 characters, logo, sameAs, foundingDate, founders and award. Keep WebSite with name 'Bellezza & Co.' and alternateName 'Bellezza Salon and Day Spa' on the homepage so Google shows the right site name.
- **BreadcrumbList:** keep it, knowing it now appears only on desktop.
- **Service and OfferCatalog:** fine to keep as entity data, but they get no rich result, and every price must match the visible price list.
- **FAQPage:** don't expect anything from it. Write FAQs as visible content for people and AI answers.
- **JobPosting:** move it to one page per job (for example jobs/massage-therapist.html). Include datePosted, a full description, hiringOrganization, jobLocation and title, plus validThrough, and baseSalary if the owners will publish it. Mark up only positions that are actually open.
- **VideoObject:** if the promo video moves from Google Drive to YouTube and is embedded, add VideoObject.
- **Check everything:** run each page through the Rich Results Test after each build.
recommendations.evidence: Google's LocalBusiness documentation says to use 'the most specific LocalBusiness sub-type possible', that multiple types go in an array, that geo needs 'at least 5 decimal places', and that priceRange must be under 100 characters. Its structured data policies say 'Don't mark up content that is not visible to readers of the page' and that rich results aren't guaranteed. FAQ rich results were limited to 'well-known, authoritative government and health websites' in August 2023, and Google confirmed 'FAQ rich results are no longer appearing in Google Search' (May 7, 2026). Breadcrumbs stopped showing on mobile on Jan 23, 2025. The JobPosting documentation says: 'Put structured data on the most detailed leaf page possible. Don't add structured data to pages intended to present a list of jobs.' The site-names documentation says 'add WebSite structured data to your home page.'

recommendations.title: Use real, well-described photos, and never AI-made or stock images that pass as the salon
recommendations.detail:
Remove the cotton and spa flatlays (hero-1/hero-2) and the candle and lily tiles from any spot that suggests they show Bellezza. Where a real image is missing, use a styled, clearly labeled placeholder, not the mockup's AI storefront or AI before/after images. Order of priority: the staff headshots, join-1 (the team), real in-service shots taken with consent, and real before/afters from stylists' Instagram used with permission from both the stylist and the client. For every image:
- Give it a short, descriptive filename, like devon-hand-sewn-extensions.jpg or bellezza-pedicure-room.jpg.
- Write alt text that describes what the photo shows, for example 'Paige painting gel nail art at Bellezza & Co.', not a keyword list.
- Place it next to the text it illustrates.
- Serve AVIF or WebP through srcset, with width and height set.

Move the words out of promo graphics like the specials and spray-tan images into real HTML text. Upload the same real photos to the Google Business Profile and keep adding new ones.
recommendations.evidence: Google's image SEO guidance calls for 'filenames that are short, but descriptive', alt text that is 'useful, information-rich... in context' without keyword stuffing, images 'placed near relevant text', srcset, and to avoid images with text. The Quality Rater Guidelines treat seeing work in progress as evidence of expertise, and deceptive content earns the Lowest rating. The FTC Act prohibits deceptive depictions. Google's local ranking tips say to 'Upload photos and videos showcasing your business'.

recommendations.title: Meet the Core Web Vitals targets on mobile: LCP 2.5s or less, INP 200ms or less, CLS 0.1 or less (75th percentile)
recommendations.detail:
How to get there:
- **Hero image:** a single AVIF/WebP with srcset/sizes, fetchpriority='high', never lazy-loaded, and explicit dimensions or aspect-ratio. Lazy-load everything below the fold.
- **Fonts:** self-host subsets of Prata and Open Sans (WOFF2, latin subset), preload the Prata weight used in the H1, and use font-display: swap with fallback metrics tuned via size-adjust to avoid layout shift.
- **Before/after carousel:** no auto-rotating carousel or heavy slider library. Use CSS scroll-snap.
- **Third parties:** load Google Maps as a static image or 'Load map' click, not an iframe on page load. Meevo booking and the Mya quiz should open as links, not embedded iframes.
- **Layout stability:** reserve space for the sticky mobile Book bar.
- Check with PageSpeed Insights and field data in Search Console.
recommendations.evidence: From web.dev: 'LCP should occur within 2.5 seconds', 'INP of 200 milliseconds or less', 'CLS of 0.1 or less', measured at 'the 75th percentile of page loads'. From Google: 'Core Web Vitals are used by our ranking systems,' but 'Google Search always seeks to show the most relevant content, even if the page experience is sub-par.' So speed helps among similar results; it won't make up for weak content.

recommendations.title: Make each service page a complete, dedicated page, without creating doorway pages
recommendations.detail:
Each service page should contain, in order:
- An H1 with the service and city.
- A two-to-three-sentence intro in first person, signed by the lead (for example 'Stephanie, Spa Manager, 20+ years' on tips-and-toes; 'Devon, Director of Education' on salon and brides).
- Prices by level (keep the .menu-group > h3 / .price-item markup that build-schema.py parses).
- Duration and what to expect at a first visit.
- Who does the service (team cards).
- Policies specific to the service, for example 'Keratin requires a consultation and $50 deposit' and 'Bridal travel team available for a fee'.
- The brands used (Dermalogica Face Mapping, Olaplex, Lakmé).
- A few real FAQs, shown on the page.
- A single Book CTA.

Add anchored sections for high-intent subservices (#balayage, #extensions, #keratin, #gel-x, #prenatal). Make a separate page only when there's enough unique content, such as hand-sewn extensions or bridal. Don't make copies of a page with only the town name changed (Heath, Granville, Pataskala), and don't add lists of towns.
recommendations.evidence: Whitespark 2026 ranks 'Dedicated Page Per Service' #1 for local organic and 'Dedicated Service Pages' #2 for AI search visibility. Google's spam policies list as doorway abuse 'pages targeted at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page', and as keyword stuffing 'Blocks of text that list cities and regions that a web page is trying to rank for'.

recommendations.title: Link pages to each other with descriptive anchor text, and keep URLs stable and consistent
recommendations.detail: Label home service tiles 'Hair color & extensions', not 'Learn more'. Team cards link to their service pages, and service pages link to their team members, Policies, Gift Cards and Book. Our Story links to the team. Every service page is linked from the header, footer and home. Add a visible breadcrumb on inner pages that matches the BreadcrumbList. Keep the current .html slugs and the _redirects map from the old WordPress URLs; don't rename URLs just for keywords. Once the host is chosen, make the canonical tags, sitemap.xml and internal links use exactly the URL form the host serves. Cloudflare Pages strips .html with a 308 redirect by default, so either link to extensionless URLs or turn that behavior off.
recommendations.evidence: Google says 'Good anchor text is descriptive, reasonably concise, and relevant to the page' and 'Every page you care about should have a link from at least one other page on your site.' Its URL guidance says to 'Add descriptive words in URL paths' and use identical URLs 'across internal links, sitemaps, and canonical tags'. Whitespark 2026 ranks 'Internal Linking Structure' #6 for local organic.

recommendations.title: Add a 'New Guests' page, since first-time visitors need the most reassurance
recommendations.detail:
The mockup's nav item 'New Guests' should link to a page covering:
- How booking works: online, app or phone.
- What the stylist levels and price tiers mean.
- The Mya matchmaking quiz, which helps a new guest pick a stylist.
- Arrival and parking.
- Etiquette: phones on silent, no speakerphone, childcare for your own appointments.
- The 24-hour change policy and the no-show escalation (reminder, then 50% deposit, then 100% prepayment).
- Gift cards.
- Contact, with the phone number as visible text.

This is both conversion copy and the customer service information raters look for.
recommendations.evidence: The Quality Rater Guidelines (sections 2.5.3 and 5.5) treat contact and customer service information as a core Trust requirement for businesses that take money. Google's helpful content 'Why' question asks whether content is 'created primarily to help people.'

recommendations.title: Publish a small set of care guides written by named staff, with bylines and dates
recommendations.detail:
Start with four to six guides from real experience rather than a stream of generic posts. Examples:
- 'Making a gel manicure last' by Paige, Expert Nail Artist
- 'Caring for hand-sewn extensions' by Devon
- 'What happens in a Dermalogica Face Mapping facial' by Emma or Mia
- 'Your bridal hair and makeup timeline' by Devon and the bridal coordinator
- 'What to expect from prenatal massage' by Jesyca, written conservatively and without medical claims

Each guide gets a byline linked to the team card, a 'Published / Updated' date, original photos, and links to the service page and Book. Link each guide from its service page. Staff can draft with help, but the named expert must review and add their own experience. Don't mass-produce AI articles.
recommendations.evidence: Google's helpful content guidance 'strongly encourage[s] adding accurate authorship information, such as bylines' and asks whether content is 'written or reviewed by an expert or enthusiast who demonstrably knows the topic well'. The Quality Rater Guidelines (sections 4.6.5 and 4.6.6) give the Lowest rating to scaled or low-effort content, including 'auto or AI generated' content with little originality.

recommendations.title: Align the Google Business Profile with the site, since it drives the local pack
recommendations.detail: Choose the primary category by revenue focus, for example 'Day spa' or 'Beauty salon', and use the same term in the homepage title and H1. Add a few accurate secondary categories (Hair salon, Nail salon, Facial spa, Waxing hair removal service, Massage spa) as long as each one is something the business is. Keep the business name exactly 'Bellezza & Co.' with no keywords added. Set the booking link to Meevo, list services with prices that match the site, and post and add photos regularly. Reply to every review personally and specifically. Ask every client for a review through a generalized request, for example a 'Leave us a Google review' link in receipts or texts. Don't offer incentives for Google reviews.
recommendations.evidence: Whitespark's 2026 top local pack factors are Primary GBP Category (#1), Keywords in GBP Business Title (#3), 4-5 star ratings (#6), additional categories (#8) and native Google reviews with text (#9). Keyword stuffing in the business name or description is a top suspension risk. Google's business name rules forbid keyword stuffing, and its category guidance says 'this business IS a...', not 'HAS a...'. BrightLocal 2026 found 80% prefer businesses that reply to all reviews, 50% are put off by templated replies, and 74% look for reviews from the last three months.

recommendations.title: Build off-site authority: best-of lists, press, vendors and schools
recommendations.detail:
Ask for listings or links from:
- The publication behind the #1 spa vote.
- Local press and the Newark/Licking County chamber.
- Brand salon locators (Dermalogica, Olaplex, Lakmé, REF, VOESH stockist pages).
- Wedding directories for bridal.
- The schools the team trained at (C-TEC, Hocking College, Paul Mitchell Columbus, Salon Institute), which fits the internship program.

Set up Apple Business Connect and make sure its details match.
recommendations.evidence: Google says prominence is 'based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have.' Whitespark 2026 ranks 'Presence on Expert-Curated Best Of Lists' #1 for AI search visibility and 'Quality Inbound Links' #3 for local organic. BrightLocal 2026 found Apple Maps usage nearly doubled.

recommendations.title: Write key facts as plain text so AI search and AI Overviews can quote them
recommendations.detail: State hours, prices, services, the founders' story, the policies and the award in HTML text, not only inside images or JSON-LD. Keep structured data identical to the visible text. Don't bother with 'AI files' or special markup.
recommendations.evidence: Google: 'There are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, nor other special optimizations necessary.' It recommends 'Making sure that important content is available in textual form' and that 'structured data matches the visible text on the page', plus keeping Business Profile information current.

recommendations.title: Make the palette readable, because contrast affects both trust and clicks
recommendations.detail:
Measured contrast:
- Body text #6b6b6b passes AA at 5.03:1 on cream #faf8f5 and 5.33:1 on white. Keep it at 16px or larger on mobile.
- Gold #b8985f fails as text on light backgrounds (2.73:1 on white). Use it for rules, icons and large display type only.
- #9c7f4c is 3.78:1 on white, so use it only for large text (24px, or 18.66px bold).

For the gold Book Now button, use ink #1c1c1c text on #b8985f (6.24:1), not white text (2.73:1). On black or ink sections, gold text works (7.69:1 on #000, 6.24:1 on #1c1c1c).
recommendations.evidence: WCAG 2.x AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; the ratios above were computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula. Google's page experience self-assessment asks whether visitors can easily tell the main content apart and whether it displays well on mobile.

recommendations.title: Help the brand stand out in results with a site name and a favicon
recommendations.detail: Add the WebSite schema name and alternateName, and match og:site_name to 'Bellezza & Co.'. Provide a square favicon at a multiple of 48px (for example the B&Co mark at 96x96 or 192x192 PNG, or an SVG) that stays legible at small sizes.
recommendations.evidence: Google's site-names documentation calls WebSite structured data 'most important' and says to keep the name consistent with og:site_name, the title and headings. Google shows favicons beside results on mobile, and its favicon guidance asks for a square image at a multiple of 48px.

recommendations.title: Put visible 'last updated' dates on prices and specials, and end dates on offers
recommendations.detail: Add 'Prices updated <Month YYYY>' under each price menu, with the value set at build time. Give every special a visible end date and remove expired ones. Put the same dates in the dateModified of the WebPage schema, and only change it when the content actually changes.
recommendations.evidence: Google's title documentation names obsolete dates as a reason to rewrite titles. The Quality Rater Guidelines treat inaccurate information as a Trust problem. BrightLocal 2026 shows consumers care strongly about freshness.

pitfalls: Publishing the mockup's invented details: phone (740) 522-4173, 200 Deo Drive, the wrong hours, staff 'Kelsey/Morgan/Abby/Tori', testimonials by 'Emily R./Jessica M./Caitlin B.', the AI before/after and storefront images, and © 2024. Each one is a Trust failure, and the testimonials would violate the FTC rule.
Filler testimonials such as 'Lorem ipsum' quotes or 'sample review' cards left on a live page. Leave the section out until real, attributed reviews exist.
Adding aggregateRating or Review markup to the business's own LocalBusiness schema, or embedding a Google review widget and expecting stars. Self-serving reviews aren't eligible.
Adding FAQPage markup for rich results. They stopped showing on May 7, 2026. FAQs still help as visible content.

Only asking happy clients for reviews through a satisfaction pre-screen, or offering discounts or entries for reviews. The FTC rule forbids rewards tied to positive reviews, and Google's policy forbids incentives for reviews at all.
Generic, templated section copy ('Welcome to our salon, where beauty meets relaxation') and stock spa imagery (towels, candles, orchids, stones). It reads as a template and shows no real experience.
Stuffing town lists ('serving Newark, Heath, Granville, Hebron, Pataskala...') or making near-identical city pages. Google's spam policies call both keyword stuffing and doorway abuse.
Adding keywords to the Google Business Profile name ('Bellezza & Co. Best Hair Salon Newark'). This is a top suspension risk.

Different name, address or phone formats in different places (Bellezza Spa, Bellezza Salon and Day Spa, Bellezza & Co; 740.366.1604 vs (740) 366-1604), or site hours that differ from the Google Business Profile and holiday hours that aren't posted.
Vague expertise claims ('highly trained experts', 'the best stylists') without names, schools, years or levels. Raters mark overstated claims as Low.
Words baked into images, such as specials graphics or hero text in a JPG. Google, screen readers and AI crawlers can't read them.
Loading the nav, footer and contact details only through JavaScript. Non-Google AI crawlers never see them, and the late insertion causes layout shift.
Heavy hero sliders, auto-playing carousels, Google Maps iframes and booking-widget iframes loading with the page. They hurt LCP and INP on phones.
White text on the #b8985f gold button (2.73:1). It fails WCAG and makes the main CTA harder to read.

Titles that use internal names ('Tips and Toes | Bellezza & Co.') instead of the words people search ('Manicures & Pedicures in Newark, OH'), or titles that don't match the H1, which leads Google to rewrite them.
Renaming URLs during the redesign without 301 redirects, or letting canonicals, the sitemap and internal links disagree about whether URLs end in .html.
Using clients' faces or stylists' Instagram photos without written permission, or using AI-generated or stock people presented as clients or staff.
Letting Slay Aesthetics' medical services read as Bellezza services, or making outcome claims without naming who provides them.
bellezza_specific: The site has no About page. Build about.html ('Our Story: Two Sisters, Newark Since 2009') from the verified timeline: born and raised in Newark, family-business upbringing, the 2008 purchase of an 1,800 sq ft house, opening in 2009, the 2022 rebrand and boutique, 5,500 sq ft today, both still behind the chair one day a week. Sign it 'Lisa & Ashley' and use their real headshots or join/join-1.jpg. Don't composite a fake photo of the two together.

The 28 consistent studio headshots are the strongest real asset for E-E-A-T. Pair each one with its verified credential line, for example: Stephanie, 'American School of Hair Design 2002, 20+ years, with Bellezza since 2010, Spa Manager since 2015'; Jesyca, 'Hocking College massage therapy degree, 2015'; Paige, 'C-TEC 2021'; Emilie, 'former cosmetology instructor, 14+ years'.

Trust bar copy the facts support: 'Est. 2009 in Newark', 'Voted #1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016' (name the source once the owners confirm it), '22 stylists, nail artists, skin and massage therapists', and 'Open 6 days, evenings until 8 Mon, Tue, Wed and Thu'.

Homepage title: 'Hair Salon & Day Spa in Newark, Ohio | Bellezza & Co.' (53 characters). Change the meta description to open with the #1 spa claim and end with 'Book online'. The current homepage description is good, but it lists services before the proof.
Retitle tips-and-toes, massages, facials, hair-removal, spray-tans and mens-care to 'Service in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.'. Keep the URLs, and keep 'Tips & Toes' as a brand label above the H1.

Have build-schema.py compute each page's lowest price from .price-item span.price and check it against any 'from $X' in the meta description. Emit holiday closures (Jan 1, Memorial Day, July 4, Labor Day, Dec 25-26, noon closings Dec 24 and 31, 5pm closings July 3 and Trick-or-Treat night) as openingHoursSpecification with validFrom/validThrough, from one holiday table that is also printed on Contact and in the footer.

The JobPosting markup is currently on jobs.html, a list of five jobs. Google wants one leaf page per job. Split it into jobs/massage-therapist.html and the others, or drop the markup. Add validThrough, and add baseSalary only if the owners approve publishing it. Benefits (paid training and assisting program, paid vacation, 401K) go in the visible description.

Keep the existing schema choices: the DaySpa/HairSalon/NailSalon array, no aggregateRating, and Slay Aesthetics as a separate MedicalBusiness. Add alternateName 'Bellezza Salon and Day Spa' to connect the old and new names, and a WebSite alternateName for the site name.
Stamp the site.js header and footer (NAP, hours, nav) into static HTML at build time, so the address and phone are in the page source for AI crawlers and there's no layout shift.

Reviews: leave the 'Real people. Real experiences.' band out at launch. Once real Google reviews exist, quote three with first name and last initial, service and month/year, and link 'Read all reviews on Google'. Check that the Meevo Five Star flow doesn't send only happy clients to Google.

The brow lamination before/after is the only real transformation image. Use it on makeup-and-eyes with its real caption. Fill the 'Transformations' band later only with consented before/afters from stylists' Instagram, credited to the stylist.
Rename generic image files when they are replaced or reused, for example services/mani-room.jpg to bellezza-manicure-room-newark.jpg, and move text out of the specials graphics into HTML.

Slay Aesthetics page: lead with 'Shannon Francis, CNP (Certified Nurse Practitioner)', say it is an independent practice inside Bellezza on Fridays 10 to 6, give the consultation-first process, note that Bellezza gift cards aren't accepted, and make no promises about results.
Book CTA button: use ink #1c1c1c text on gold #b8985f (6.24:1), keep a sticky Book bar on mobile, and put a one-line policy note ('24-hour notice for changes · Policies') right next to it.

Move the promo video from Google Drive to YouTube. Embed it on Our Story with a click-to-load facade and add VideoObject markup, since Drive-hosted video isn't a practical source for Google video results.

Before launch, confirm the Google Business Profile name reads exactly 'Bellezza & Co.', check the primary category, set the booking link to Meevo, make sure service prices match the site, and add holiday Special Hours for the next 12 months.

dimension: Competitive teardown: 13 salon, spa and beauty sites (national premium brands plus Midwest independents similar to Bellezza), and the patterns the best ones share

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Glowbar (glowbar.com), the benchmark for mobile booking
recommendations.detail: HERO: full-bleed photo of a real face with visible skin texture. On mobile the headline and copy sit BELOW the photo rather than on top of it: eyebrow 'FACE YOUR SKIN WITH', headline '30-Minute Custom Glowbar Facials', then a short promo paragraph and a full-width 'BOOK NOW' button. BOOKING: the header stays pinned on mobile with Menu, Logo, Cart and an outlined 'BOOK' button, so booking is one tap away at every scroll depth (checked at 390px after scrolling 2,500px: header BOOK still visible). SERVICES/PRICES: one product at two prices, '$95 for Non-Members' and '$75 for Members', described as 'no add-ons ever'. The service page lists what may be included (peels, extractions, microcurrent, LED). TEAM: expertise is stated as scale: 'over three quarters of a million facials across almost 30 studios', 'Skincare experts, not false promises'. TRUST: press logos (CNN, Coveteur and others), three reviews with full names, and an Instagram results feed under #afterglowbar. STYLE: warm off-white background, one saturated accent used ONLY for booking actions, big friendly sans serif, generous spacing. BORROW: (1) keep a visible 'Book' button in the mobile header, not inside the hamburger menu; (2) stack the image above the text on mobile so the headline is never set over a busy photo. AVOID: the H1 is empty (the headline is not marked up as H1), which wastes the page's most valuable SEO heading.
recommendations.evidence: Playwright check at 390x844: the fixed header element holds 'Cart BOOK'; the H1 array returned [""]. The mobile screenshot shows the photo, then the text, then a full-width CTA.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Heyday (heydayskincare.com), the benchmark for putting numbers on expertise
recommendations.detail: HERO: an offer headline, '$40+ off your first facial', with 'Book your first Essential Facial and see what your skin's been missing.' and 'BOOK AND SAVE NOW', over a photo of a treatment in progress. BOOKING: a pill-shaped 'BOOK' button in the mobile header next to search, bag, account and menu; 'Book a Facial' repeats in every section; 'Manage Appointments' goes to Boulevard. SERVICES: four named facials. The service page gives the price by tier (Monthly Member $125 / Bimonthly $130 / Non-Member $155), the duration ('50-minute treatment'), and four numbered steps: skin analysis, custom treatment, personal skincare plan, guidance for between visits. TEAM: 'The most trusted hands'. Numbers do the work: '100+ hours of advanced Heyday training', '5yrs of experience on average, above industry norms', '80% of returning clients request the same Esthetician', '92% of our reviews are 5 stars', 'over 1 million Heyday facials'. Each esthetician profile has a photo, studio, favorite treatment and a first-person philosophy line ('I specialize in treating acne and aging skin...'). TRUST: before-and-after pictures organized by skin concern (acne, dehydration, texture, dark spots). STYLE: cream-to-butter gradients, navy type, soft rounded buttons, calm and editorial. BORROW: (1) give each team member a specialty and a one-line philosophy in their own words; (2) show every service as price + duration + 3-4 numbered 'what happens' steps. AVOID: the discount leads the hero, and on mobile the cookie banner covers the lower half of the first screen, CTA included. It feels transactional, which is wrong for a relationship business.
recommendations.evidence: WebFetch of the home, the-essential-facial and our-experts pages, plus a Playwright mobile screenshot showing the cookie banner over the hero CTA.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Drybar Shops (drybarshops.com), the benchmark for a visual menu of outcomes
recommendations.detail: HERO: 'NO CUTS. NO COLOR. JUST BLOWOUTS!', a single-sentence positioning line. BOOKING: 'BOOK NOW / BOOK YOUR BLOWOUT' goes to a location finder, with a Book tab in the top nav and an app download. SERVICES: the menu is a set of named RESULTS ('The Manhattan: straight, sleek and smooth', 'The Mai Tai: effortless, messy, beachy'), each with a photo carousel and 'Show This Model' buttons that switch between models with different hair types, plus a 'Book This Style' button on every style. TEAM: none shown (franchise model). TRUST: brand fame, a membership offer, and '$10 off your first blowout' for email signup. STYLE: yellow and white, playful cocktail names. BORROW: (1) sell outcomes, not procedures: a 'Looks' gallery (lived-in blonde, hand-sewn extensions, special-occasion updo), each linking to the matching service and stylist; (2) show each look on several hair types. AVOID: the live homepage still shows Latin placeholder copy ('Sed ut perspiciatis unde omnis iste natus...') under 'GET THE BOOKING APP!'. Placeholders that reach production destroy trust, and the Bellezza mockup has placeholder slots that are at risk of the same thing.
recommendations.evidence: Playwright text extraction of drybarshops.com returned the lorem ipsum paragraph verbatim; the-styles page shows 'Book This Style' and 'Show This Model' controls on each style.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Rescue Spa (rescuespa.com), the benchmark for founder authority and service-page structure
recommendations.detail: HERO: a treatment headline, 'Lift, Sculpt & Glow', with one sentence of benefit copy and paired CTAs, 'Book Now' + 'Shop Your Routine'. BOOKING: 'BOOK NOW' is the last item in the nav; buttons on each service book by city ('Book In New York' / 'Book In Philadelphia'). SERVICES: category tiles with photos; separate price-list pages for each city. Each single service page has: a description, who it is for ('great for first-timers', 'perfect for regulars'), a step list (assessment, product selection, extractions, massage, mask), a list of benefits and concerns treated, and a 'Send As Gift' button next to Book. TEAM: a 'Meet Danuta' founder block: 30+ years, master esthetician, a philosophy quote ('Beautiful skin is a matter of choice, not chance.'), and a YouTube video of her demonstrating her method. TRUST: press quotes naming the publication ('Best Spa in New York City' - Vogue; 'Best Facials in New York City' - Goop). STYLE: clean luxury, white space, restrained serif. BORROW: (1) put a 'Give this as a gift' button next to Book on every service page; (2) a founder block built on an in-her-own-words quote plus years in the chair. AVOID: no durations or prices on the service pages; pricing is pushed to a separate list or the booking engine, which adds a step at the point of decision.
recommendations.evidence: WebFetch of the homepage, the about page and the products/rescue-facial service page.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Mizu Louis Licari (mizuforhair.com), an acclaimed NYC independent
recommendations.detail: HERO: 'WELCOME TO Mizu Louis Licari' with the CTA 'Learn More About Us'. The primary hero CTA is not booking. BOOKING: a 'Book Now' button top right, a 'Book Services' CTA under the hero, gift cards in the header. SERVICES: six cards (Haircut and Styling, Color, Make Up, Smoothing, Perm, Men's Grooming), no prices: 'Pricing varies by stylist and service level', 'Priced upon Consultation', 'Complimentary consultation required' (color correction). TEAM: titles carry the specialty ('Curly Hair Specialist', 'Perm Specialist', 'Master Colorist'). TRUST: 5-star testimonials with names and specific detail ('I fly out from the West Coast twice a year'). STYLE: white type on dark, minimal. BORROW: specialty-bearing titles, the kind Bellezza already has in its facts (e.g. Devon: hand-sewn extensions and blonding; Raegan: pedicure specialist). Show them as chips. AVOID: hiding prices entirely. It suits Manhattan luxury, but for a Newark, Ohio guest price uncertainty is the top reason to leave without booking, and Bellezza already publishes its prices by level.
recommendations.evidence: WebFetch of the homepage and /services/.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Nine Zero One (ninezeroonesalon.com), celebrity LA salon
recommendations.detail: HERO: 'Home of the #901girl' + 'Book Appointment', over a carousel of celebrity and red-carpet work. BOOKING: the nav splits booking into lines of business ('901 Salon', '901 Weddings', 'SKJ Airbrush Tan'), and weddings get their own email (weddings@901salon.com). The actual booking page is only 'To request an appointment, email frontdesk@...' plus a 'Request appointment' button to Phorest. SERVICES: no prices anywhere. TRUST: 'since 2009', press, an Academy. STYLE: black and white, carousel-heavy. BORROW: make bridal a separate funnel with its own contact route (Bellezza has a bridal coordinator email, dsabo@bellezzaspaonline.com, and a travel team). AVOID: carousels as the main hero content (autoplay slides get little attention after the first slide), and a booking page that only says 'email us'.
recommendations.evidence: WebFetch of the homepage and /pages/book.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Bluemercury Spa and Sally Hershberger (weaker references)
recommendations.detail: BLUEMERCURY SPA: hero reads 'Bluemercury Spa' plus one line tying the spa to the products it sells ('same level of efficacy and results as the products sold in our stores'); a 'Book Now' button; four service cards (Facials: 'Fifty-minute, personalized...'; Brow Styling; Chemical Peels: 'Thirty-minute treatments...'; seasonal PCA facial). No prices, no esthetician credentials, no reviews. BORROW: putting the duration inside the one-line description ('Fifty-minute...') is an easy way to set expectations. SALLY HERSHBERGER: the site is now almost entirely about the 24K product line, with press logos (NYT, Refinery29, WWD) and no booking. AVOID (both): generic 'expert aestheticians' claims with nothing behind them. Unsupported expertise adds nothing to E-E-A-T.
recommendations.evidence: WebFetch of bluemercury.com/pages/bluemercury-spa-near-me and sallyhershberger.com.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Blondie's Salon & Spa, Columbus, IN (the closest analog to Bellezza; Salon Today 200 2025)
recommendations.detail: Same shape of business as Bellezza: founded 2008 by owner Lindsey Babinec, a 10,000 sq ft salon + spa + boutique, 30+ team members, gold-on-black palette. HERO: a headline in spaced capitals, 'EXPERIENCE REJUVENATION', over a photo of the interior; H1 'Come relax in an exceptional setting, take home a confidence that lasts.'; gold buttons 'MAKE APPOINTMENT' + 'WATCH VIDEO TOUR'. BOOKING: 'BOOK ONLINE' via Phorest plus 'BOOK A CONSULT'; a virtual consultation form for new clients. SERVICES: four big tiles (Salon/Hair, Spa/Face & Body, Med Spa, Boutique), with the boutique treated as a peer of the services. Prices are 'starting at' figures ('ALL-OVER COLOR $150+', 'NEW CLIENT CUT $100+') and the method is explained: 'pricing is based on the time needed to complete your service'. Stylist tiers are named (Rising, Protege, Studio, Master, Director of Education & Culture). TRUST: '4.8/5 across 874 reviews (Google 4.8 / 812)', a 'Rate Your Visit' prompt, an amenities list (robes, wine, cappuccino, hydration station). Home sections include 'Things to Know: BEFORE YOUR VISIT / YOUR FIRST VISIT'. BORROW: (1) a 'Your first visit' block (arrival, consult, what to bring, policies in plain words); (2) a boutique tile in the services grid and a video-tour CTA. AVOID: on a 390px phone the stacked black header (gift button, logo, hamburger, 5 social icons, Book button) is about 360px tall, over 40% of the first screen, and it does not stick, so no Book button is visible after scrolling (all 5 booking links returned vis:false at 2,500px).
recommendations.evidence: Playwright mobile screenshot plus scroll check; WebFetch of the home and hair-services pages. Salon Today 200 2025 lists Blondie's.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Rejuve Aveda Salon Spa, Carmel, IN (5-time Salon Today 200)
recommendations.detail: HERO: the H1 names the city: 'Rejuve Aveda Salon & Spa - Luxury Hair, Skin & Spa Services in Carmel, IN'; dual CTAs 'book now' + 'purchase gift card'. BOOKING: 'book now' sits inside a sticky nav bar, but on mobile it is only reachable through the MENU hamburger; the phone number is a tel: link (3 on the page). SERVICES: range pricing that reflects stylist level, e.g. 'Signature Haircut: $49.00 - $111.00', 'Curl & Coils Haircut: $83.00 - $175.00', with a 'Learn About Our Levels' link. There are 6 levels (Master, Senior, Designer, Studio, New Talent, Licensed Apprentice), but the staff page lists only names and titles: no photos, no bios. TRUST: Salon Today 200 badge, BBB badge, one named testimonial; a strong in-house portrait shoot of real clients (four consistent studio portraits in a grid). SCHEMA: LocalBusiness + HairSalon/BeautySalon + BreadcrumbList. BORROW: (1) price ranges tied to levels with a one-click level explainer; (2) a gift-card CTA beside Book in the hero. AVOID: overlay pile-up. At 390px the auto-opened chatbot ('Hello, I am Mira!'), the cookie banner, the UserWay accessibility bubble and an Aveda sticky together cover roughly 40% of the screen.
recommendations.evidence: Playwright: the fixed elements list shows userway, aveda-sticky, smartbot-pane (auto 'show') and the cookie banner; screenshot confirms. WebFetch of /cut-and-style and /staff.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: Revive Salon & Day Spa, Findlay, OH (Salon Today 200 2025, Best of Ohio)
recommendations.detail: HERO: an SEO-first H2 'Professional Hair Services & Luxury Spa Services in Findlay', subhead 'Tailored Beauty & Wellness Services', 'Book Now' (Phorest). SERVICES: eight category cards (Day Spa Packages, Salon, Extensions, Head Spa, Facials, Massage, Sauna, Brows); 'Starting at' prices on the service pages ('Women's Haircut: Starting at $50', 'Consultation: Starting at $25'); named packages ('The Revived Glow', 'The Total Transformation'). TEAM: 'Meet Our Passionate Experts', 10 profiles with role labels (Owner & Master Stylist, Esthetician). TRUST: 'Award-Winning for Best of Ohio, Top 200 Salon in the U.S.', a 5-star testimonial section, 'Proudly a Davines Salon & Comfort Zone Day Spa', The Knot bridal badge. LOCAL: city in headings, address, hours, Google Map; schema HealthAndBeautyBusiness. BORROW: (1) naming the partner brands as a credential ('Proudly a Davines Salon'), which for Bellezza would be 'Dermalogica skin center with Face Mapping' language, only if accurate; (2) a bridal trust badge and a preview-appointment offer for brides. AVOID: after scrolling on mobile the only 'Book Now' is off-screen (vis:false) while a third-party chat bubble floats; the booking CTA does not follow the user.
recommendations.evidence: Playwright scroll check at 390px; WebFetch of the home and salon-services pages; Salon Today 200 2025 list.

recommendations.title: TEARDOWN: The Spa at River Ridge (Dublin, OH) and PENZONE Salons + Spas (Columbus, OH): regional competitors
recommendations.detail: RIVER RIDGE: the hero is a seasonal gift-certificate promo ('GIVE THE GIFT OF RELAXATION...' + 'SHOP NOW'); 'BOOK NOW' in the top nav; categories in the nav (Hair, Extensions, Skin, Body, Nails) with no prices on the home page; an owner bio (Peigi Hanson, quoted in the first person); the team menu is split by discipline (Hair Stylists, Estheticians, Massage Therapists, Manicurists, Management); community giving is quantified ('$35,000' donated in 2025); teal accents. PENZONE: the hero IS the award ('We're honored to be named the 2026 Columbus CEO Best of Business Spa/Salon!', 'Best Hair Salon + Best Spa!') paired with an unrelated winter-apparel product photo; an offer of '25% OFF any service that's NEW TO YOU'; 6 Columbus locations. BORROW: (1) a team page filtered by discipline (Bellezza: Hair / Nails / Skin / Massage / Aesthetics / Guest Services); (2) naming the award AND who gave it, as Penzone does ('Columbus CEO Best of Business'). AVOID: letting a seasonal promo or an award notice take over the hero. The hero should say what Bellezza is and offer booking; promos belong in a slim bar or a band further down.
recommendations.evidence: WebFetch of both homepages.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 1: Booking is one tap away at every scroll depth on mobile
recommendations.detail: The best sites (Glowbar, Heyday) keep a compact header pinned on mobile with a labeled 'Book' button outside the hamburger menu. The weaker ones (Blondie's, Revive, Rejuve on mobile) lose it or hide it. For Bellezza: keep a slim sticky header (about 56-64px) showing the logo, a 'Book' button (ink text on gold, 44px minimum touch target) and the menu. Optionally, from 60% of the first screen onward, add a bottom action bar on phones with two actions, 'Book' and 'Call', using env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Never show both the sticky header CTA and a bottom bar CTA saying the same thing; choose one on phones. Every Book link goes directly to the Meevo URL (https://login.meevo.com/bellezza/ob?locationId=103245), not to an intermediate page, unless that page adds real value (see Pattern 5).
recommendations.evidence: Glowbar fixed header 'Cart BOOK' visible after a 2,500px scroll; Heyday 'BOOK' pill in the header; Blondie's and Revive have 0 visible booking links after scrolling; Rejuve's is in the hamburger menu.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 2: The hero shows a real person mid-service, says in one line what the business is and where, and has one primary CTA
recommendations.detail: Across all 13 sites, the heroes that work show a real face or hands mid-treatment (Glowbar, Heyday) with a single clear CTA. Heroes that are a logo (Mizu, Sally Hershberger), an interior (Blondie's), a promo (River Ridge, Heyday) or an award notice (Penzone) do less. For Bellezza: H1 in Prata that states the offer AND the place (e.g. 'Hair, nails, skin and massage in Newark, Ohio', or the owner's line 'Beauty & relaxation, tailored to you.' with 'Newark's salon, spa & boutique since 2009' as the eyebrow). Then one gold 'Book an appointment' button and one text-link secondary ('Explore services'), a one-line trust note under the buttons ('Voted #1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016'), and a photo on the right (desktop) or top (mobile) with no text over it. Until a real mid-service photo exists, use the real full-team photo (join-1.jpg) or a strong headshot, not the cotton/towel stock image and not an AI image.
recommendations.evidence: Glowbar mobile stacks the image above text with a full-width CTA; Heyday uses a treatment close-up; Mizu and Sally Hershberger use logo-only heroes with no booking CTA; Penzone's award headline sits on an unrelated product photo.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 3: Expertise is proven with specifics (numbers, credentials, specialties), not adjectives
recommendations.detail: Heyday ('100+ hours of advanced training', '5yrs average experience', '80% request the same esthetician') and Rescue ('30+ years', 'master esthetician') turn expertise into facts; Bluemercury's generic 'expert aestheticians' conveys nothing. Bellezza has real specifics to use: 'Since 2009', '28 team members', 'Voted #1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016', a Director of Education (Devon), and training credentials per person (C-TEC, Hocking College 2015 massage therapy degree, Paul Mitchell The School Columbus, Salon Institute, American School of Hair Design 2002), plus years (Stephanie 20+ years, joined 2010; Moriah nearly two decades; Emilie 14+ years, former cosmetology instructor), a Certified Nurse Practitioner (Shannon Francis CNP), and a paid training and assisting program. Present them as: a trust bar with 3-4 facts; on each team card, level + specialty chips + school/year; on service pages, 'Who does this service' with 2-4 portraits. Do not add up years across people or invent percentages.
recommendations.evidence: Heyday our-experts page; Rescue about page; Bluemercury spa page has no specifics.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 4: Local winners show prices and explain the level system; only Manhattan and LA luxury hide them
recommendations.detail: Every Midwest top performer shows prices: Rejuve ranges ('$49.00 - $111.00') plus 'Learn About Our Levels'; Blondie's '$150+' plus a one-line explanation of how prices are set; Revive 'Starting at $50'. The price-hiding sites are NYC/LA luxury (Mizu, Nine Zero One, Rescue). Bellezza already has prices by level, so make them the most usable of the set. On the services overview, show 'from $X' per category. On each service page, keep the .menu-group > h3 / .price-item structure (build-schema.py depends on it) but add: a level-legend row (Jr Associate / Associate / Senior / Expert / Master) with a one-line meaning each; a clear price range; the duration wherever it is known (massage 30-75 min); and a note on which services need a consultation (keratin: consultation + $50 deposit). Neither Rejuve nor Blondie's explains its levels on the price page itself, so doing this inline is an easy lead.
recommendations.evidence: Rejuve /cut-and-style, Blondie's hair-services, Revive salon-services; Mizu uses 'Pricing varies by stylist and service level' / 'Priced upon Consultation'.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 5: A clear path for first-time guests, with the consultation offered as a first step
recommendations.detail: Blondie's ('Things to Know / BEFORE YOUR VISIT / YOUR FIRST VISIT', 'BOOK A CONSULT', virtual consultation form), Rejuve ('New to Rejuve') and Mizu ('Complimentary consultation required') all separate new guests from regulars. For Bellezza (the mockup nav already has 'New Guests'): build a New Guests page and home band with (1) 'Not sure who to book? Take the 2-minute match quiz' linking to https://app.joinmya.com/bellezza; (2) 'How our levels work' (prices by level); (3) 'Your first visit': arrival, parking at 206 Deo Drive, the consult, what to bring; (4) policies in plain language (24h notice, the cancellation escalation, the quiet-salon etiquette); (5) Book and Call. This page is also where a nervous first-timer decides to book.
recommendations.evidence: Blondie's homepage headings include 'Things to Know', 'BEFORE YOUR VISIT', 'YOUR FIRST VISIT'; Rejuve nav 'New to Rejuve'; Heyday's discount and Penzone's '25% OFF any service that's NEW TO YOU' show that competitors single out first visits.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 6: Single-service pages follow the same outline: what it is, who it's for, what happens, price and duration, who does it, book or gift
recommendations.detail: The strongest service pages (Heyday Essential Facial, Rescue Facial, Glowbar services) use this order: 1) name + one-line benefit; 2) price + duration; 3) 'what happens' in 3-5 numbered steps; 4) who it's for or concerns treated ('great for first-timers', 'perfect for regulars'); 5) the practitioner; 6) Book + 'Send As Gift'. For Bellezza's 10 category pages: add an intro that says who the page is for, a 'what to expect' strip, the price menu (existing markup), 'Your artists for this service' (2-4 team cards linking to our-team dialogs), policies that apply (e.g. Slay Aesthetics does not accept Bellezza gift cards), a short FAQ drawn only from real policy facts, then Book + eGift (https://na0.meevo.com/EgiftApp/home?tenantId=100947).
recommendations.evidence: Heyday lists 4 steps with price per tier and '50-minute treatment'; Rescue has steps, a 'who it's for' line, concerns treated and 'Send As Gift'; Glowbar lists the included modalities.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 7: Awards and review counts are specific, attributed and verifiable
recommendations.detail: Rescue names the publication for every accolade ('Best Spa in New York City' - Vogue). Penzone names the awarding body (Columbus CEO Best of Business). Blondie's gives a count and a source ('4.8 across 874 reviews; Google 4.8/812'). Vague claims weaken the signal. For Bellezza: 'Voted #1 spa in Licking County every year since 2016' should name who ran the vote (e.g. a local newspaper's readers' choice), and the owner needs to supply that fact; ideally link to or show the badge. For reviews: until real ones are collected, show NO testimonial cards. Instead run a 'Loved your visit? Rate us' band linking to the Meevo Five Star page and the Google review link, and add review snippets later, verbatim and with permission. Do not mark up first-party reviews as AggregateRating on the LocalBusiness schema; Google does not show stars for self-serving LocalBusiness/Organization reviews.
recommendations.evidence: Rescue press list; Penzone hero; Blondie's review aggregate; the mockup's testimonials (Emily R./Jessica M./Caitlin B.) are fabricated and must not be used.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 8: Local SEO: city in the H1 and title, LocalBusiness schema, real NAP and hours
recommendations.detail: The Midwest winners put the city in the H1/title (Rejuve '...in Carmel, IN'; Revive '...in Findlay'; Blondie's title 'Salon & Spa Columbus IN') and publish LocalBusiness-family JSON-LD (Rejuve HairSalon/BeautySalon; Revive HealthAndBeautyBusiness), a tel: link and the hours. Glowbar ships an empty H1. For Bellezza: exactly one H1 per page containing the service + 'Newark, Ohio' where natural; title pattern '<Service> in Newark, OH | Bellezza & Co.'; keep build-schema.py output as DaySpa/BeautySalon with geo 40.086310,-82.422132, openingHoursSpecification and special holiday hours; add tel:740-366-1604 in the header on mobile; put the visit block (address, hours with today's hours highlighted, map link) on every page footer.

recommendations.title: PATTERN 9: Owner and founder story told with specifics and an in-their-own-words quote

pitfalls: Placeholder text or images reaching production. Drybar Shops' live homepage shows Latin placeholder copy ('Sed ut perspiciatis...'); any 'photo coming soon' or lorem block from the Bellezza mockup must either be real content or be left out.

Overlay pile-up on mobile. At 390px, Rejuve's auto-opening chatbot, cookie banner, UserWay accessibility bubble and brand sticky together cover about 40% of the screen. Bellezza should ship no chat widget, no accessibility overlay widget (build accessibility in), and no cookie banner unless tracking truly requires one.
Tall mobile headers. Blondie's stacked header is about 360px tall (over 40% of the first screen) and does not stick; keep Bellezza's mobile header to one slim row with a visible Book button.
Hiding the Book button in the hamburger menu or losing it on scroll (Rejuve on mobile, Revive and Blondie's after scrolling).

Promo- or award-led heroes (Heyday discount, River Ridge gift promo, Penzone award text over an unrelated product photo). Put offers in a slim bar or a band further down; the hero states who, what, where and how to book.
Logo-only or carousel heroes with no booking CTA (Mizu 'Learn More About Us', Sally Hershberger, Nine Zero One carousel).
Empty or duplicate H1s (Glowbar's H1 is empty; Rejuve has two H1s). Use one descriptive H1 per page.
Vague expertise claims ('expert aestheticians') with no credentials, years, schools or specialties behind them.
Unattributed awards. 'Voted #1' without naming who ran the vote reads like marketing; get the source from the owners.
Fabricated or unverifiable social proof: mockup testimonials, AI before/afters, AI storefront, invented stats, or self-serving AggregateRating schema.
Stock spa flatlays (cotton, towels, candles, lilies). None of the top sites use them and they read as template.
Hiding prices the way Manhattan luxury salons do. For a Newark, Ohio audience, price transparency is a conversion advantage and the Midwest winners all show prices.
Booking pages that only say 'email us' (Nine Zero One). Every Book action should open Meevo online booking directly.
